1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 180-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

value.full_target:
The complete Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with its Section 2 standing definitions and fixed scheme, on PDF page 2.

Use the periodic domain mathbbT = reals/(2*pi*integers) with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). For a periodic function f, hat f(k) = (2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx and <k> = (1+k^2)^(1/2). The Sobolev norm is ||f||_(H^s)^2 = sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s) |hat f(k)|^2. These spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms, with negative-order spaces interpreted as distributions. Reality means hat f(-k) = conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0) = 0. Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms use essential suprema.

Let S_t = exp(-t*partial_x^3), with Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3). Let P0 be the spatial mean and P = I-P0. Let D^(-1) = partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k != 0 and zero at k=0, and D^(-2) = (D^(-1))^2. The equation is
  u_t + u_xxx = (1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0.
The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation.

For timestep tau=T/L, the time-semidiscrete scheme is exactly
  u^0 = u0,
  u^(n+1) = S_tau u^n + F_tau(u^n) + H_tau(u^n),
where all products below are spatial products and [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0):
  F_tau(f) = (1/6)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)^2]
             - (1/6)*S_tau P[(D^(-1) f)^2],
  H_tau(f) = (1/3)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)*D^(-1) F_tau(f)]
             + (tau/9)*(S_tau D^(-1) f)*P0(f^2)
             - (1/54)*[S_(tau-s) D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1) f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
             - (1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s D^(-1) f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
This is the source scheme (2), with no spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0, there exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, this fixed scheme satisfies
  max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2) <= C*tau^gamma.
The constants are uniform over the entire stated initial-data ball and all permitted timesteps, with no Fourier-support restriction. The target includes all the hypotheses, quantifiers, endpoints, solution convention and method above.
value.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique distributional solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) obtained by smooth approximation and the fixed unfiltered iterates of Psi satisfy max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_L2<=C*tau^gamma for every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. The constants are uniform over that entire datum ball and all these L; no Fourier-support restriction is imposed.

definitions.definition: mathbbT=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi).

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx. The transform extends by completion to Sobolev spaces and by distributional duality. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

definitions.type: family of Fourier Sobolev spaces and norms
definitions.definition: For real s, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2), ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials, interpreted as distributions for negative s; L2=H^0 with the normalized spatial norm. On mean-zero functions ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Time suprema use continuous representatives and derivative norms essential suprema. For sequences x, ||x||_(ell2)^2=sum_k |x(k)|^2; ell1 uses sum_k |x(k)|. Frequency projections P_{<=A}, P_{>A} retain respectively |k|<=A and |k|>A.
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k), for every real t.
P0 f=hat f(0), identified with the constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1): its multiplier is (i*k)^(-1) at k!=0 and zero at k=0. D^(-2)=Dinv composed with Dinv. Spatial derivatives use multiplier i*k.
For tau>0 and periodic f in L2, F_tau(f)=(1/6)*P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

For tau>0 and periodic f in L2, H_tau(f)=(1/3)*P[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv F_tau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Every product is spatial and [G(s)]_0^tau=G(tau)-G(0).

definitions.type: unfiltered time-step map and its iterates
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+F_tau(f)+H_tau(f). For positive integer L set tau=T/L and t_n=n*tau. Define u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L. There is no spatial cutoff in this recurrence.
For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

For tau>0, t_n=n*tau and k!=0, hat(R2_(n,tau)(f1,f2,f3))(k)= -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Output at k=0 is zero. Initially this formula is on Fourier polynomials; bounded extension is proved below. Terms with a zero input frequency vanish since one phase is zero.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)].
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t) P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].
For I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b, Cint_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t) P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))}dt; time-independent inputs are read as constant paths.
p_star=23/14. For an interval I of length at most one, ||f||_X(I)=||f||_(L^infty(I;L2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infty(I;H^(-p_star))).

binders.type: time path with the displayed norms finite

definitions.definition: For 0<gamma<=1, a_gamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2; a_gamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2; and a_gamma=0 if gamma>1/2.

For tau>0, nonnegative integer n, t_n=n*tau and t in [t_n,t_n+tau], Stage_(n,tau)(t;f)= (1/2) integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f,f)ds, initially for a time-independent smooth mean-zero f; the endpoint normal form below gives its L2 extension.

For smooth mean-zero step data f at t_n=n*tau, write F_n(t)=Stage_(n,tau)(t;f), z_n=f+F_n, C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f,F_n(s))ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(F_n(s),F_n(s))ds, W_n=Q_n(t_n+tau)+R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f), V_n(t)=f+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau, Y_n=V_n-z_n, rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau. For f=S_(-t_n)u^n, concatenate V_n as V and the increments rho_n as Rres, with Rres(0)=0. Continuity of V at grid points is a proved property, not an assumption.

definitions.type: normalized periodic KdV equation and exact-solution convention
definitions.definition: KdV is the equation u_t+partial_x^3 u=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on mathbbT. For a real mean-zero datum q in H^s, s>=0, and horizon A>0, an exact solution u with datum q means the real mean-zero C([0,A];H^s) distributional solution of this equation with u(0)=q obtained by smooth approximation. An exact twisted solution v means v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) for this same equation and interval. A smooth exact solution means such a solution with smooth space and time dependence. These terms specify a solution relation only; existence, uniqueness, bounds and the differential equation for the twist are proved, rather than granted by this definition.

value.representation_notes: One representation throughout: a Coeff is the normalized complex Fourier coefficient sequence indexed by ℤ, with conjugate symmetry for reality and coefficient zero at zero for mean zero. H s is weighted square summability with weight (1+k²)^s, and hn is the square root of that sum; dh/dn are the homogeneous versions restricted away from zero. This is exactly the completion-of-polynomials model in D003, including negative orders. contH and convH state continuity/convergence in these weighted norms, not pointwise coefficient topology. smooth means membership in every nonnegative integer Sobolev space, equivalent to a smooth periodic function; smoothCurve and smoothPair express norm continuity and C¹ dependence at every such order. All displayed series and integrals are mathematical noncomputable definitions; consumers must establish the guarded summability, integrability and boundedness, which are included in the output obligations when substantive. No default tsum or sSup value is used as an analytic conclusion without the appropriate domain. mul is spatial multiplication in coefficients, air is S_t, and invD is zero on mode zero. The unfiltered scheme and finite iterates are explicit formulas, with no unspecified solver or algebraic capabilities. weakD is the coefficientwise integrated weak derivative with the absolutely continuous representative. aeH supplies coefficient measurability, a.e. Hilbert membership and an essential bound; separability of weighted ℓ² identifies this with the usual Bochner L∞ condition. essH uses ENNReal essential supremum then toReal only on these bounded domains; xn uses essential norms, while supH concerns actual continuous value representatives. piecewise allows separate derivative extensions at knots and identifies the global derivative only a.e. on each piece. solution uses the physical normalized equation's coefficient integral identity; for s≥0 C H^s this is equivalent to the distributional equation because the L² product has absolutely convergent convolution coefficients. exact adds uniform-in-time L² convergence from smooth solutions for the Fourier cutoffs of q, expressing the fixed smooth-approximation solution convention without granting existence. Uniqueness is EqOn on [0,T], so arbitrary values of a Curve outside its horizon never affect the result. sign=1 denotes target u_t+u_xxx=∂x(u²)/2, sign=-1 denotes the source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx; this is an actual equation-sign parameter, not a regularity assumption. No M ports or background-note premises are introduced. Native type probes verified these complete predicates with no missing parameters. The ℝ powers in the weights and estimates are Real.rpow; natural powers of complex Fourier multipliers are ordinary monoid powers. The membership predicate uses real Summable rather than overloading an lp parameter: the inspected Memℓp definition uses an ENNReal exponent (zero means finite support and infinity means boundedness), so neither is silently used as Sobolev order. All frequency indices and grid indices are explicitly ℤ and ℕ respectively; n≥0 is intrinsic to ℕ, and L>0 is a proposition, not a truncated integer division. Complex scalar action on coefficients is pointwise; real coefficients in scalar actions are explicitly cast to ℂ.

steps.explanation: Exact-flow transfer. Apply E001 to the sign-reflected coefficients -q(-k), preserving reality, zero mean and every homogeneous norm. Check the inverse reflection and the physical equation's linear sign, then compare homogeneous and inhomogeneous weights on k≠0, in both exponent directions. For a smooth datum use all positive integer regularities and uniqueness. Unimodularity proves the twist norm identity and differentiating smooth solutions gives weakD of the twist with B/2. Establish the single ball bound before quantifying q. For arbitrary L² pairs apply θ=0 dependence and undo the unitary twists/reflection; the L² constant depends only on T and the summed norm bound.

Prove the scalar covariance estimates by cancellation, the fundamental theorem of calculus and either integration by parts, retaining both phase ratios. For a nonzero zero-sum quartet prove the ordered-magnitude cases, including ties. List.Perm plus the displayed inequalities states precisely what an ordering means; all denominators here are nonzero. The max/min formula k3 used in the next node is exactly the third largest magnitude, even with ties.

Dyadically decompose nonnegative sequences supported away from zero. For each ordering, the largest two shell indices differ by at most two. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the large pair and the cardinalities of the small shells produce 2^(-(j3-j4)/2) after division by the third largest frequency. Sum the geometric factor and the finitely many orderings/offsets. Pass from finite restrictions by monotone convergence. Summability and the bound are asserted together for each arbitrary subset Ω, avoiding the default value of an unsummable real tsum.

Combine T002's two multiplier majorants by geometric interpolation for 0≤s≤1; duality and T003 give the uniform trilinear estimate with any modulus≤1 multiplier, including either resonance restriction. Prove absolute coefficient summability and complex trilinearity, then density gives the unique bounded extension from polynomial inputs. The finite formula and its extension therefore use the same rem definition. Finally telescope the diagonal cubic at f around w: use exponent gamma only at (w,w,w) and exponent zero on the difference terms. No H^gamma norm of f is assumed.

Fourier isometry and elementary inverse-derivative, H¹ embedding and product estimates supply linearBounds, with H membership of each output explicit. Products denote convolution, justified by Cauchy-Schwarz or absolute summability of inverse-derivative coefficients. For the normal form differentiate the phase on smooth inputs, prove the coefficient identity, and integrate retaining both endpoints. For piecewise paths sum over a finite partition; derivatives are only identified a.e. with the piecewise extensions, so jumps do not require a common endpoint derivative. Prove symmetry, the cubic integral identity without commuting a product through an operator, and the constant-input stage identity.

Normalize E002 by srcScale=√(2π), including the value and derivative components of X; its alpha=0 instance is exactly the normalized variable-path bound. E003 with epsilon=1/8 and gamma>0 gives the chosen aux exponent and product estimate. Choose a single admissible sufficiently small epsilon_stage≤1/8 for the midpoint application of E004, before any state or step is chosen. Check the three beta0 cases and positive denominators: beta=aux gamma yields a time power at least gamma and beta=1+gamma yields power zero. Since 0<tau≤1 the weaker tau^gamma estimate follows. Constants are uniform in interval position, n, tau and support.

From E005 and the explicitly defined physical update, prove the twisted endpoint identity and preservation of smoothness, reality and mean zero. Check the S_(s-tau) factor in the last endpoint term. Differentiate the interpolation on each step, expand V=z+Y, and identify the actual residual derivative drho. Prove weakD for the concatenated paths, continuity and finite piecewise smoothness, both grid values, Y's initial zero value, and the concatenated residual increments. idx uses floor(t/tau) for nonnegative times; at grid endpoints either adjacent formula agrees by the proved endpoint identities.

Under the stated step hypothesis put q=tau^gamma+‖f-w‖₂≤2. T005's endpoint stage formula gives the uniform H¹ bound and the H¹ difference from Stage(w); T006 gives the small low-regularity norm. Split the derivative of the exact-data square using the product estimate, and control the square difference in H¹. T004 bounds the actual numerical-state remainder in W. Split f=w+(f-w) to bound Dinv B(f,F), integrate Y' from its initial zero value, and use the cubic normal form for C_n with the time-independent and mixed exponent-zero bounds. All displayed H memberships, admissibility and X bounds follow from these estimates and smooth step data.

Apply the existing normal form to (Y,z) and then (Y,Y), retaining both endpoints. Use T008's Dinv Y and Dinv Y' bounds with the asymmetric J estimate, and T006's negative-slot cubic estimate for the differentiated z term. Bound q² by 2q. The affine W contribution is the actual W of the interpolation. This gives the L² bound for rho; the negative-norm bilinear estimate applied directly to drho gives its essential derivative bound. No global residual is substituted for the step formula.

Take any smooth solution of the normalized equation, twist it and differentiate its coefficient equation. For e=v-V establish e'=B(e,v-e/2)-Rres' and the X bounds under E_I≤1. Sum actual step residual increments, allowing a final partial step. Split the integrated bilinear error at real frequency N≥2. Low output costs N²h. At high output apply the normal form retaining the initial endpoint; rewrite differentiated terms as the two Cint terms and the integral of J(Rres',V). Split each cubic input at N/3; all-low input frequencies cannot reach output >N, while each designated high slot has negative norm ≤C N^(-23/14) times its L² norm. Treat the forcing integral with the actual stepwise drho, Y and W bounds. Combine to obtain exactly the stated conditional stability inequality. The constant is uniform for solutions with 1+sup‖v‖_(H^gamma)≤M and depends only on T,gamma,M.

Use T001's common ball bound, and the normalized smooth equation required by T010. Choose N first to absorb its reciprocal powers, then a block length delta and tau≤delta/2. On blocks of floor(delta/tau) grid steps iterate the absorbed inequality. Continuity from T007 and the exact flow supports the first-hitting-time contradiction; the estimate also covers a prefix ending inside a step. Choose tau0 uniformly so the resulting K tau0^gamma<1/2. The interpolation bound implies the grid bound by the actual grid identity and isometry. The constants are chosen before any smooth datum or positive integer L.

Approximate q by low m q, preserving reality, mean zero and the H^gamma ball. T001 gives exact solutions converging uniformly in L². For each fixed tau>0 prove continuity in L² of the fully specified step using T005's inverse-derivative and H¹ product bounds; then all finitely many iterates converge. Apply T011 with the same constants to every cutoff datum. Pass the reverse triangle inequality at all n≤L and then their finite maximum. Retain existence and uniqueness in the smooth-approximation solution class. Constants precede q and L; no numerical Sobolev bound or cutoff is introduced into the method.

1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.

88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.

92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.

102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.

121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.

129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large

131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in

148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided

import Mathlib
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal
open MeasureTheory Filter Set
noncomputable section
namespace KdV
abbrev Coeff := ℤ → ℂ
abbrev Curve := ℝ → Coeff
def weight (s : ℝ) (k : ℤ) : ℝ := (1 + (k : ℝ)^2) ^ s
def H (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Prop := Summable (fun k => weight s k * ‖f k‖^2)
def hn (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (∑' k, weight s k * ‖f k‖^2)
def dh (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Prop :=
  f 0 = 0 ∧ Summable (fun k : ℤ => if k = 0 then 0 else |(k : ℝ)|^(2*s) * ‖f k‖^2)
def dn (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (∑' k : ℤ, if k = 0 then 0 else |(k : ℝ)|^(2*s) * ‖f k‖^2)
def realCoeff (f : Coeff) : Prop := ∀ k, f (-k) = star (f k)
def mz (f : Coeff) : Prop := f 0 = 0
def data (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Prop := H s f ∧ mz f
def rd (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Prop := data s f ∧ realCoeff f
def smooth (f : Coeff) : Prop := ∀ m : ℕ, H (m : ℝ) f
def poly (f : Coeff) : Prop := Set.Finite (Function.support f)
def ik (k : ℤ) : ℂ := Complex.I * (k : ℂ)
def air (t : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  fun k => Complex.exp (Complex.I * (t : ℂ) * (k : ℂ)^3) * f k
def proj (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => if k = 0 then 0 else f k
def mean (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => if k = 0 then f 0 else 0
def invD (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => if k = 0 then 0 else (ik k)⁻¹ * f k
def invD2 (f : Coeff) : Coeff := invD (invD f)
def dx (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => ik k * f k
def mul (f g : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => ∑' a : ℤ, f a * g (k-a)
def cube (f : Coeff) : Coeff := mul (mul f f) f
def low (N : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => if |(k : ℝ)| ≤ N then f k else 0
def high (N : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff := f - low N f
def eval (f : Coeff) (x : ℝ) : ℂ := ∑' k : ℤ, Complex.exp (Complex.I * (k : ℂ) * (x : ℂ)) * f k
def linfty (f : Coeff) : ℝ := sSup ((fun x => ‖eval f x‖) '' Icc 0 (2*Real.pi))
def bn (t : ℝ) (f g : Coeff) : Coeff := air (-t) (dx (mul (air t f) (air t g)))
def jn (t : ℝ) (f g : Coeff) : Coeff := air (-t) (proj (mul (air t (invD f)) (air t (invD g))))
def cint (a b : ℝ) (f g h : Curve) : Coeff :=
  fun k => ∫ t in a..b, (air (-t) (proj (mul (proj (mul (air t (f t)) (air t (g t)))) (air t (invD (h t)))))) k
def intC (a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : Coeff := fun k => ∫ t in a..b, f t k
def stage (n : ℕ) (τ t : ℝ) (f g : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  (1/2 : ℂ) • intC ((n : ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r f g)
def favg (τ α : ℝ) : ℂ := (τ : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..τ, Complex.exp (-Complex.I * (t : ℂ) * (α : ℂ))
def eta (τ α β : ℝ) : ℂ := favg τ (α+β) - favg τ α * favg τ β
def phase1 (a b : ℤ) : ℝ := 3*(a:ℝ)*(b:ℝ)*((a+b):ℤ)
def phase2 (k c p : ℤ) : ℝ := 3*(k:ℝ)*(c:ℝ)*(p:ℝ)
abbrev Mult := ℤ → ℤ → ℤ → ℤ → ℂ
def unitMult : Mult := fun _ _ _ _ => 1
def rterm (μ : Mult) (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f g h : Coeff) (k : ℤ) (v : ℤ × ℤ) : ℂ :=
  let a := v.1
  let b := v.2
  let c := k-a-b
  let α := phase1 a b
  let β := phase2 k c (a+b)
  if k = 0 ∨ a+b = 0 then 0 else
    -(τ : ℂ)/(18*ik k) * μ k a b c *
      Complex.exp (-Complex.I * ((n:ℝ)*τ : ℝ) * ((α+β : ℝ) : ℂ)) *
      eta τ α β * f a * g b * h c
def rem (μ : Mult) (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f g h : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  fun k => ∑' v : ℤ × ℤ, rterm μ n τ f g h k v
def quad (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  (1/6 : ℂ) • proj (mul (air τ (invD f)) (air τ (invD f))) -
  (1/6 : ℂ) • air τ (proj (mul (invD f) (invD f)))
def cubic (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  let F := quad τ f
  let E := fun s => air (τ-s) (invD (cube (air s (invD f))))
  let G := fun s => air (τ-s) (invD2 (mul (air (s-τ) (invD2 F)) (air s (invD f))))
  (1/3 : ℂ) • proj (mul (air τ (invD f)) (invD F)) +
  ((τ/9 : ℝ) : ℂ) • mul (air τ (invD f)) (mean (mul f f)) -
  (1/54 : ℂ) • (E τ - E 0) - ((1/(27*τ) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (G τ - G 0)
def step (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff := air τ f + quad τ f + cubic τ f
def iter (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : ℕ → Coeff
  | 0 => q
  | n+1 => step τ (iter τ q n)
def pstar : ℝ := 23/14
def aux (γ : ℝ) : ℝ := if γ < 1/2 then 1/2-γ else if γ = 1/2 then 1/8 else 0
def sourceAux (s ε : ℝ) : ℝ := if s = 0 then 1/2+ε else if s < 1/2 then 1/2-s else if s = 1/2 then ε else 0
def beta0 (s ε : ℝ) : ℝ := if s < 1/2 then 2*s-3/2 else if s = 1/2 then -1/2-ε else s-1
def k3 (a b c d : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  max (min |(a:ℝ)| (min |(b:ℝ)| |(c:ℝ)|))
    (max (min |(a:ℝ)| (min |(b:ℝ)| |(d:ℝ)|))
      (max (min |(a:ℝ)| (min |(c:ℝ)| |(d:ℝ)|)) (min |(b:ℝ)| (min |(c:ℝ)| |(d:ℝ)|))))
def contH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, H s (f t)) ∧
  ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧
    ∀ r ∈ Icc a b, |r-t| < δ → hn s (f r - f t) < ε
def convH (s : ℝ) (f : ℕ → Coeff) (g : Coeff) : Prop :=
  (∀ n, H s (f n)) ∧ H s g ∧ Tendsto (fun n => hn s (f n-g)) atTop (nhds 0)
def supH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : ℝ := sSup ((fun t => hn s (f t)) '' Icc a b)
def boundedH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, H s (f t)) ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, hn s (f t) ≤ C
def aeH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : ℤ, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun t => f t k) (volume.restrict (Icc a b))) ∧
  (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc a b)), H s (f t)) ∧
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc a b)), hn s (f t) ≤ C
def essH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : ℝ :=
  (essSup (fun t => ENNReal.ofReal (hn s (f t))) (volume.restrict (Icc a b))).toReal
def weakD (a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : ℤ, IntervalIntegrable (fun t => df t k) volume a b) ∧
  ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ∀ k : ℤ, f t k = f a k + ∫ r in a..t, df r k
def admissible (s a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : Prop :=
  aeH s a b f ∧ aeH (-pstar) a b df ∧ weakD a b f df
def xn (a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : ℝ := essH 0 a b f + essH (-pstar) a b df
def normDeriv (s a b t : ℝ) (f : Curve) (d : Coeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ r ∈ Icc a b,
    0 < |r-t| → |r-t| < δ →
      hn s (f r - f t - ((r-t : ℝ) : ℂ) • d) ≤ ε * |r-t|
def smoothPair (a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : ℕ, contH (m:ℝ) a b f ∧ contH (m:ℝ) a b df ∧
    ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, normDeriv (m:ℝ) a b t f (df t)
def piecewise (a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : ℕ, contH (m:ℝ) a b f) ∧
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ → ℝ, ∃ d : ℕ → Curve,
    r 0 = a ∧ r N = b ∧
    (∀ j < N, r j ≤ r (j+1) ∧ smoothPair (r j) (r (j+1)) f (d j) ∧
      (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc (r j) (r (j+1)))), df t = d j t))
def twisted (sign : ℝ) (u : Curve) : Curve := fun t => air (-sign*t) (u t)
def rhs (sign : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  fun k => Complex.I * (sign : ℂ) * (k : ℂ)^3 * f k + (1/2 : ℂ) * ik k * mul f f k
def solution (sign s A : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (u : Curve) : Prop :=
  contH s 0 A u ∧ u 0 = q ∧
  (∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, realCoeff (u t) ∧ mz (u t)) ∧
  (∀ k : ℤ, IntervalIntegrable (fun t => rhs sign (u t) k) volume 0 A) ∧
  ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, ∀ k : ℤ, u t k = q k + ∫ r in (0:ℝ)..t, rhs sign (u r) k
def smoothCurve (a b : ℝ) (u : Curve) : Prop := ∀ m : ℕ, contH (m:ℝ) a b u
def exact (sign s A : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (u : Curve) : Prop :=
  solution sign s A q u ∧ ∃ us : ℕ → Curve,
    (∀ m : ℕ, solution sign 0 A (low (m:ℝ) q) (us m) ∧ smoothCurve 0 A (us m)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun m => supH 0 0 A (fun t => us m t-u t)) atTop (nhds 0)
end KdV

namespace KdV
def srcScale : ℝ := Real.sqrt (2*Real.pi)
def pairing (f g : Coeff) : ℂ := ∑' k : ℤ, f k * star (g k)
def L1dual (s A : ℝ) (g : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : ℤ, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun t => g t k) (volume.restrict (Icc 0 A))) ∧
  (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc 0 A)), dh (-s) (g t)) ∧
  IntegrableOn (fun t => dn (-s) (g t)) (Icc 0 A) volume
def gal (A : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (m : ℕ) (u : Curve) : Prop :=
  u 0 = low (m:ℝ) q ∧ smoothCurve 0 A u ∧
  (∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, rd 0 (u t) ∧ low (m:ℝ) (u t) = u t) ∧
  weakD 0 A u (fun t => low (m:ℝ) (rhs (-1) (u t)))
def galBounds : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ B Q : ℝ, 0 ≤ B → 0 ≤ Q →
  ∃ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M ∧ ∀ q : Coeff, dh s q → realCoeff q → hn 0 q ≤ B → dn s q ≤ Q →
    ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ u : Curve, gal A q m u → ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, dn s (u t) ≤ M
def sourceCompactness : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ q : Coeff, dh s q → realCoeff q →
  ∀ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ < s →
  ∃ us : ℕ → Curve, ∃ u : Curve, ∃ κ : ℕ → ℕ,
    (∀ m, gal A q m (us m)) ∧ StrictMono κ ∧ exact (-1) s A q u ∧
    (∃ M : ℝ, (∀ m t, t ∈ Icc 0 A → dn s (us m t) ≤ M) ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, dn s (u t) ≤ M) ∧
    (∀ p : ℝ, 1 < p →
      Tendsto (fun j => ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..A, hn σ (us (κ j) t-u t)^p) atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
    (∀ g : Curve, L1dual s A g →
      Tendsto (fun j => ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..A, pairing (us (κ j) t) (g t)) atTop
        (nhds (∫ t in (0:ℝ)..A, pairing (u t) (g t))))
def sourceFlow : Prop :=
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ q : Coeff, dh s q → realCoeff q →
    ∃ u : Curve, exact (-1) s A q u ∧
      (∀ v : Curve, solution (-1) s A q v → EqOn u v (Icc 0 A)) ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, hn 0 (u t) = hn 0 q) ∧
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B →
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ q r : Coeff,
      dh s q → dh s r → realCoeff q → realCoeff r → dn s q + dn s r ≤ B →
      ∀ u v : Curve, exact (-1) s A q u → exact (-1) s A r v →
        ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, dn s (u t-v t) ≤ C*dn s (q-r)) ∧
  (∀ θ B : ℝ, -1 < θ → θ ≤ 0 → 0 ≤ B →
    ∃ C D : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < D ∧
      ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ q r : Coeff,
        rd 0 q → rd 0 r → hn 0 q+hn 0 r ≤ B →
        ∀ u v : Curve, exact (-1) 0 A q u → exact (-1) 0 A r v →
          ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A,
            dn θ (twisted (-1) u t-twisted (-1) v t) ≤ C*D^A*dn θ (q-r))
def sourceUniform : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ B Q : ℝ, 0 ≤ B → 0 ≤ Q →
  ∃ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M ∧ ∀ q : Coeff, dh s q → realCoeff q → hn 0 q ≤ B → dn s q ≤ Q →
    ∀ u : Curve, exact (-1) s A q u → ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, dn s (u t) ≤ M
def bit : Prop := galBounds ∧ sourceCompactness ∧ sourceFlow ∧ sourceUniform
def cubicBounds (K : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ α a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → b-a ≤ 1 →
    ∀ f df : Fin 3 → Curve, (∀ j, admissible α a b (f j) (df j)) →
      H 0 (cint a b (f 0) (f 1) (f 2)) ∧ ∀ i : Fin 3,
      K*hn 0 (cint a b (f 0) (f 1) (f 2)) ≤
        C*(b-a)*(∏ j : Fin 3, K*xn a b (f j) (df j)) +
        C*(K*essH (-pstar) a b (f i))*
          (∏ j ∈ (Finset.univ.erase i), K*essH 0 a b (f j))) ∧
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → b-a ≤ 1 →
    ∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, H s (f j)) →
      H 0 (cint a b (fun _ => f 0) (fun _ => f 1) (fun _ => f 2)) ∧
      K*hn 0 (cint a b (fun _ => f 0) (fun _ => f 1) (fun _ => f 2)) ≤
        C*(b-a)^s*(∏ j : Fin 3, K*hn s (f j)))
def productBounds (K : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 →
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ f g : Coeff, H s f → H (sourceAux s ε) g →
    H 0 (mul f g) ∧ K*hn 0 (mul f g) ≤ C*(K*hn s f)*(K*hn (sourceAux s ε) g)
def stageBoundAt (K s ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ β : ℝ, beta0 s ε ≤ β → β ≤ 1+s →
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ t : ℝ, 0 < τ →
  t ∈ Icc ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) →
  ∀ f g : Coeff, data s f → data s g →
    H β (stage n τ t f g) ∧
    K*hn β (stage n τ t f g) ≤
      C*τ^((1+s-β)/(1+s-beta0 s ε))*(K*hn s f)*(K*hn s g)
def stageBounds (K : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ 1 → s ≠ 1/2 → stageBoundAt K s 0) ∧
  ∃ ε0 : ℝ, 0 < ε0 ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < ε0 → stageBoundAt K (1/2) ε
def schemeIdentity : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → ∀ f : Coeff, smooth f → mz f →
    air (-((n:ℝ)*τ)-τ) (step τ (air ((n:ℝ)*τ) f)) =
      f + stage n τ (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) f f +
      intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) (fun t => bn t f (stage n τ t f f)) -
      rem unitMult n τ f f f
def fn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => stage n τ t f f
def zn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => f + fn n τ f t
def dz (f : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t f f
def cn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r f (fn n τ f r))
def qn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => (1/2 : ℂ) • intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r (fn n τ f r) (fn n τ f r))
def wn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  qn n τ f (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) + rem unitMult n τ f f f
def vn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => f + fn n τ f t + cn n τ f t + qn n τ f t -
    (((t-(n:ℝ)*τ)/τ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
def yn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve := vn n τ f - zn n τ f
def dy (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => bn t f (fn n τ f t) + (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (fn n τ f t) (fn n τ f t) -
    ((τ⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
def drho (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => -bn t (yn n τ f t) (zn n τ f t) -
    (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (yn n τ f t) (yn n τ f t) -
    ((τ⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
def rho (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => -intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r (yn n τ f r) (zn n τ f r)) -
    (1/2 : ℂ) • intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r (yn n τ f r) (yn n τ f r)) -
    (((t-(n:ℝ)*τ)/τ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
def idx (τ t : ℝ) : ℕ := (Int.floor (t/τ)).toNat
def datum (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (n : ℕ) : Coeff := air (-((n:ℝ)*τ)) (iter τ q n)
def interp (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => vn (idx τ t) τ (datum τ q (idx τ t)) t
def residual (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : Curve := fun t =>
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (idx τ t), rho j τ (datum τ q j) (((j:ℝ)+1)*τ)) +
    rho (idx τ t) τ (datum τ q (idx τ t)) t
def dres (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => drho (idx τ t) τ (datum τ q (idx τ t)) t
def dvnum (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : Curve := fun t =>
  let n := idx τ t
  let f := datum τ q n
  (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (zn n τ f t) (zn n τ f t) - ((τ⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
end KdV

namespace KdV
def phaseEst : Prop :=
  ∀ τ α β : ℝ, 0 < τ →
    ((α = 0 ∨ β = 0) → eta τ α β = 0) ∧
    (α ≠ 0 → β ≠ 0 →
      ‖eta τ α β‖ ≤ 2*min |α/β| |β/α| ∧
      ‖eta τ α β‖ ≤ τ*min |α| |β|)
def freqEst : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c d : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → d ≠ 0 → a+b+c+d = 0 →
  ∀ N1 N2 N3 N4 : ℝ,
    List.Perm [|(a:ℝ)|, |(b:ℝ)|, |(c:ℝ)|, |(d:ℝ)|] [N1,N2,N3,N4] →
    N4 ≤ N3 → N3 ≤ N2 → N2 ≤ N1 →
    N1 ≤ 3*N2 ∧
    |(d:ℝ)|⁻¹ * min (|(a:ℝ)*(b:ℝ)|/|(c:ℝ)*(d:ℝ)|)
      (|(c:ℝ)*(d:ℝ)|/|(a:ℝ)*(b:ℝ)|) ≤ 3/N3 ∧
    |((a+b:ℤ):ℝ)| / max |(a:ℝ)*(b:ℝ)| |(c:ℝ)*(d:ℝ)| ≤ 6/N3
def phaseAndGeometry : Prop := phaseEst ∧ freqEst
def quadTerm (x : Fin 4 → ℤ → ℝ) (Ω : Set (ℤ × ℤ × ℤ)) (v : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) : ℝ :=
  let a := v.1
  let b := v.2.1
  let c := v.2.2
  let d := -(a+b+c)
  @ite ℝ (v ∈ Ω ∧ a ≠ 0 ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ c ≠ 0 ∧ d ≠ 0)
    (Classical.propDecidable (v ∈ Ω ∧ a ≠ 0 ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ c ≠ 0 ∧ d ≠ 0))
    (x 0 a * x 1 b * x 2 c * x 3 d / k3 a b c d) 0
def fourLinear : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x : Fin 4 → ℤ → ℝ,
    (∀ j, x j 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ k, 0 ≤ x j k) ∧ Summable (fun k => (x j k)^2)) →
    ∀ Ω : Set (ℤ × ℤ × ℤ),
      Summable (quadTerm x Ω) ∧
      (∑' v, quadTerm x Ω v) ≤ C*(∏ j : Fin 4, Real.sqrt (∑' k, (x j k)^2))
def triOn (s : ℝ) (G : (Fin 3 → Coeff) → Coeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j)) → ∀ i : Fin 3,
    (∀ u v : Coeff, data s u → data s v →
      G (Function.update f i (u+v)) = G (Function.update f i u) + G (Function.update f i v)) ∧
    (∀ u : Coeff, data s u → ∀ c : ℂ,
      G (Function.update f i (c • u)) = c • G (Function.update f i u))
def triBound (s τ C : ℝ) (G : (Fin 3 → Coeff) → Coeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j)) →
    H 0 (G f) ∧ hn 0 (G f) ≤ C*τ^(1+s)*(∏ j : Fin 3, hn s (f j))
def remainderCore : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
  ∀ μ : Mult, (∀ k a b c, ‖μ k a b c‖ ≤ 1) →
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ →
    let G := fun f : Fin 3 → Coeff => rem μ n τ (f 0) (f 1) (f 2)
    triOn s G ∧ triBound s τ C G ∧
    (∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j)) →
      ∀ k : ℤ, Summable (rterm μ n τ (f 0) (f 1) (f 2) k)) ∧
    (∀ F : (Fin 3 → Coeff) → Coeff, triOn s F →
      (∃ D : ℝ, 0 < D ∧ triBound s τ D F) →
      (∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j) ∧ poly (f j)) → F f = G f) →
      ∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j)) → F f = G f)
def numericalRemainder (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → τ ≤ 1 →
  ∀ f w : Coeff, data 0 f → data γ w → hn γ w ≤ M → hn 0 (f-w) ≤ 1 →
    H 0 (rem unitMult n τ f f f) ∧
    hn 0 (rem unitMult n τ f f f) ≤ C*τ*(τ^γ+hn 0 (f-w))
def remainderBounds (γ : ℝ) : Prop := remainderCore ∧ numericalRemainder γ
def linearBounds : Prop :=
  (∀ s t : ℝ, ∀ f : Coeff, H s f → H s (air t f) ∧ hn s (air t f) = hn s f) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ f : Coeff, (realCoeff f → realCoeff (air t f)) ∧ (mz f → mz (air t f))) ∧
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    (∀ f : Coeff, data 0 f → H 1 (invD f) ∧ hn 1 (invD f)+linfty (invD f) ≤ C*hn 0 f) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ f g : Coeff, data 0 f → data 0 g →
      H (-pstar) (bn t f g) ∧ hn (-pstar) (bn t f g) ≤ C*hn 0 f*hn 0 g ∧
      H 1 (jn t f g) ∧ hn 1 (jn t f g) ≤ C*hn 0 f*hn 0 g) ∧
    (∀ f : Coeff, H 1 f → linfty f ≤ C*hn 1 f) ∧
    (∀ f g : Coeff, H 1 f → H 1 g →
      H 1 (mul f g) ∧ hn 1 (mul f g) ≤ C*hn 1 f*hn 1 g) ∧
    (∀ f g : Coeff, H 0 f → H 0 g →
      H 0 (invD (proj (mul f g))) ∧ hn 0 (invD (proj (mul f g))) ≤ C*hn 0 f*hn 0 g) ∧
    (∀ f : Coeff, mz f → H 0 (invD f) →
      H (-pstar) f ∧ hn (-pstar) f ≤ hn 0 (invD f)) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ f g : Coeff, mz f → H 0 (invD f) → H 0 g →
      H 0 (jn t f g) ∧ hn 0 (jn t f g) ≤ C*hn 0 (invD f)*hn 0 g)
def normalForms : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ f g : Coeff, data 0 f → data 0 g → jn t f g = jn t g f) ∧
  (∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → ∀ f df g dg : Curve,
    piecewise a b f df → piecewise a b g dg →
    (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, mz (f t) ∧ mz (g t)) →
    intC a b (fun t => bn t (f t) (g t)) =
      (1/3 : ℂ) • (jn b (f b) (g b)-jn a (f a) (g a)) -
      (1/3 : ℂ) • intC a b (fun t => jn t (df t) (g t)+jn t (f t) (dg t))) ∧
  (∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → ∀ f g h : Curve,
    smoothCurve a b f → smoothCurve a b g → smoothCurve a b h →
    (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, mz (f t) ∧ mz (g t) ∧ mz (h t)) →
    intC a b (fun t => jn t (bn t (f t) (g t)) (h t)) = cint a b f g h) ∧
  (∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ t : ℝ, 0 < τ →
    t ∈ Icc ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) → ∀ f : Coeff, data 0 f →
    stage n τ t f f = (1/6 : ℂ) • (jn t f f - jn ((n:ℝ)*τ) f f))
def basic : Prop := linearBounds ∧ normalForms
def normalizedProduct (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ f g : Coeff, H γ f → H (aux γ) g →
    H 0 (mul f g) ∧ hn 0 (mul f g) ≤ C*hn γ f*hn (aux γ) g
def normalizedStages (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
  ∀ w : Coeff, data γ w → hn γ w ≤ M → ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ t : ℝ, 0 < τ → τ ≤ 1 →
  t ∈ Icc ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) →
    H (aux γ) (stage n τ t w w) ∧ hn (aux γ) (stage n τ t w w) ≤ C*τ^γ ∧
    H (1+γ) (stage n τ t w w) ∧ hn (1+γ) (stage n τ t w w) ≤ C
def continuousBounds (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 ≤ aux γ ∧ aux γ < 1 ∧ cubicBounds 1 ∧ normalizedProduct γ ∧ normalizedStages γ
def flow (T γ R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∃ A : ℝ, 0 ≤ A ∧ ∀ q : Coeff, rd γ q → hn γ q ≤ R →
    (∃ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u) ∧
    (∀ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u →
      (∀ v : Curve, solution 1 γ T q v → EqOn u v (Icc 0 T)) ∧
      (smooth q → smoothCurve 0 T u) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T, hn γ (u t) ≤ A) ∧
      supH γ 0 T (twisted 1 u) ≤ A ∧
      (∀ s t : ℝ, t ∈ Icc 0 T → H s (u t) →
        H s (twisted 1 u t) ∧ hn s (twisted 1 u t) = hn s (u t)) ∧
      (smooth q → weakD 0 T (twisted 1 u)
        (fun t => (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (twisted 1 u t) (twisted 1 u t))))) ∧
  (∀ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ q r : Coeff,
    rd 0 q → rd 0 r → hn 0 q+hn 0 r ≤ B →
    ∀ u v : Curve, exact 1 0 T q u → exact 1 0 T r v →
      supH 0 0 T (u-v) ≤ C*hn 0 (q-r))
def interpolation : Prop :=
  ∀ q : Coeff, smooth q → realCoeff q → mz q → ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ →
    (∀ n : ℕ, smooth (iter τ q n) ∧ realCoeff (iter τ q n) ∧ mz (iter τ q n)) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, interp τ q ((n:ℝ)*τ) = datum τ q n) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, yn n τ (datum τ q n) ((n:ℝ)*τ) = 0) ∧
    (∀ L : ℕ, piecewise 0 ((L:ℝ)*τ) (interp τ q) (dvnum τ q) ∧
      weakD 0 ((L:ℝ)*τ) (interp τ q) (dvnum τ q) ∧
      weakD 0 ((L:ℝ)*τ) (residual τ q) (dres τ q)) ∧
    residual τ q 0 = 0 ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
      dvnum τ q t = (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (interp τ q t) (interp τ q t) + dres τ q t) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, ∀ t ∈ Icc ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ),
      residual τ q t-residual τ q ((n:ℝ)*τ) = rho n τ (datum τ q n) t)
end KdV

namespace KdV
def stepHyp (γ M τ : ℝ) (f w : Coeff) : Prop :=
  smooth f ∧ smooth w ∧ mz f ∧ mz w ∧ H γ w ∧ hn γ w ≤ M ∧ hn 0 (f-w) ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < τ ∧ τ ≤ 1
def stepControlsAt (γ C : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f w : Coeff) : Prop :=
  let a := (n:ℝ)*τ
  let b := ((n:ℝ)+1)*τ
  let δ := hn 0 (f-w)
  let q := τ^γ+δ
  admissible 0 a b (zn n τ f) (dz f) ∧
  admissible 0 a b (yn n τ f) (dy n τ f) ∧
  xn a b (zn n τ f) (dz f) ≤ C ∧
  xn a b (yn n τ f) (dy n τ f) ≤ C*q ∧
  H 0 (wn n τ f) ∧ hn 0 (wn n τ f) ≤ C*τ*q ∧
  ∀ t ∈ Icc a b,
    H 1 (fn n τ f t) ∧ hn 1 (fn n τ f t) ≤ C ∧
    H 1 (fn n τ f t-stage n τ t w w) ∧ hn 1 (fn n τ f t-stage n τ t w w) ≤ C*δ ∧
    H (aux γ) (fn n τ f t) ∧ hn (aux γ) (fn n τ f t)+hn 0 (fn n τ f t) ≤ C*q ∧
    H 0 (bn t (fn n τ f t) (fn n τ f t)) ∧ hn 0 (bn t (fn n τ f t) (fn n τ f t)) ≤ C*q ∧
    H 0 (qn n τ f t) ∧ hn 0 (qn n τ f t)+hn 0 (wn n τ f) ≤ C*τ*q ∧
    H 0 (invD (yn n τ f t)) ∧ hn 0 (invD (yn n τ f t)) ≤ C*τ*q ∧
    H 0 (invD (dy n τ f t)) ∧ hn 0 (invD (dy n τ f t)) ≤ C*q ∧
    H 0 (yn n τ f t) ∧ hn 0 (yn n τ f t) ≤ C*q ∧
    H (-pstar) (yn n τ f t) ∧ hn (-pstar) (yn n τ f t) ≤ C*τ*q
def stepControls (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 1 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ,
    ∀ f w : Coeff, stepHyp γ M τ f w → stepControlsAt γ C n τ f w
def residualControls (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 1 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ,
  ∀ f w : Coeff, stepHyp γ M τ f w →
    let a := (n:ℝ)*τ
    let b := ((n:ℝ)+1)*τ
    let q := τ^γ+hn 0 (f-w)
    boundedH 0 a b (rho n τ f) ∧ supH 0 a b (rho n τ f) ≤ C*τ*q ∧
    aeH (-pstar) a b (drho n τ f) ∧ essH (-pstar) a b (drho n τ f) ≤ C*q
def stability (T γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 1 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
  ∀ q : Coeff, ∀ u : Curve, solution 1 γ T q u → smoothCurve 0 T u →
    1+supH γ 0 T (twisted 1 u) ≤ M →
  ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → τ ≤ 1 →
  ∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → b ≤ T → b-a ≤ 1 →
    (∃ n : ℕ, a = (n:ℝ)*τ) →
    let e := twisted 1 u - interp τ q
    let E := supH 0 a b e
    E ≤ 1 → ∀ N : ℝ, 2 ≤ N →
      E ≤ hn 0 (e a)+C*(b-a+τ)*τ^γ+
        C*(N^2*(b-a)+(b-a)+τ+N⁻¹+N^(-pstar))*E
def gridRate (T γ C τ0 : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (u : Curve) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : ℕ, 0 < L →
    let τ := T/(L:ℝ)
    τ ≤ τ0 → ∀ n : ℕ, n ≤ L →
      H 0 (iter τ q n) ∧
      hn 0 (u ((n:ℝ)*τ)-iter τ q n) ≤ C*τ^γ
def smoothRate (T γ R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C τ0 : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < τ0 ∧
    ∀ q : Coeff, rd γ q → smooth q → hn γ q ≤ R →
    (∃ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u) ∧
    (∀ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u →
      gridRate T γ C τ0 q u ∧
      ∀ L : ℕ, 0 < L →
        let τ := T/(L:ℝ)
        τ ≤ τ0 → supH 0 0 T (twisted 1 u - interp τ q) ≤ C*τ^γ)
def rate (T γ R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C τ0 : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < τ0 ∧
    ∀ q : Coeff, rd γ q → hn γ q ≤ R →
    (∃ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u ∧
      ∀ v : Curve, exact 1 γ T q v → EqOn u v (Icc 0 T)) ∧
    (∀ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u → gridRate T γ C τ0 q u)
end KdV

value.statement: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique distributional solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) obtained by smooth approximation and the fixed unfiltered iterates of Psi satisfy max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_L2<=C*tau^gamma for every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. The constants are uniform over that entire datum ball and all these L; no Fourier-support restriction is imposed.

results.value: One representation throughout: a Coeff is the normalized complex Fourier coefficient sequence indexed by ℤ, with conjugate symmetry for reality and coefficient zero at zero for mean zero. H s is weighted square summability with weight (1+k²)^s, and hn is the square root of that sum; dh/dn are the homogeneous versions restricted away from zero. This is exactly the completion-of-polynomials model in D003, including negative orders. contH and convH state continuity/convergence in these weighted norms, not pointwise coefficient topology. smooth means membership in every nonnegative integer Sobolev space, equivalent to a smooth periodic function; smoothCurve and smoothPair express norm continuity and C¹ dependence at every such order. All displayed series and integrals are mathematical noncomputable definitions; consumers must establish the guarded summability, integrability and boundedness, which are included in the output obligations when substantive. No default tsum or sSup value is used as an analytic conclusion without the appropriate domain. mul is spatial multiplication in coefficients, air is S_t, and invD is zero on mode zero. The unfiltered scheme and finite iterates are explicit formulas, with no unspecified solver or algebraic capabilities. weakD is the coefficientwise integrated weak derivative with the absolutely continuous representative. aeH supplies coefficient measurability, a.e. Hilbert membership and an essential bound; separability of weighted ℓ² identifies this with the usual Bochner L∞ condition. essH uses ENNReal essential supremum then toReal only on these bounded domains; xn uses essential norms, while supH concerns actual continuous value representatives. piecewise allows separate derivative extensions at knots and identifies the global derivative only a.e. on each piece. solution uses the physical normalized equation's coefficient integral identity; for s≥0 C H^s this is equivalent to the distributional equation because the L² product has absolutely convergent convolution coefficients. exact adds uniform-in-time L² convergence from smooth solutions for the Fourier cutoffs of q, expressing the fixed smooth-approximation solution convention without granting existence. Uniqueness is EqOn on [0,T], so arbitrary values of a Curve outside its horizon never affect the result. sign=1 denotes target u_t+u_xxx=∂x(u²)/2, sign=-1 denotes the source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx; this is an actual equation-sign parameter, not a regularity assumption. No M ports or background-note premises are introduced. Native type probes verified these complete predicates with no missing parameters. The ℝ powers in the weights and estimates are Real.rpow; natural powers of complex Fourier multipliers are ordinary monoid powers. The membership predicate uses real Summable rather than overloading an lp parameter: the inspected Memℓp definition uses an ENNReal exponent (zero means finite support and infinity means boundedness), so neither is silently used as Sobolev order. All frequency indices and grid indices are explicitly ℤ and ℕ respectively; n≥0 is intrinsic to ℕ, and L>0 is a proposition, not a truncated integer division. Complex scalar action on coefficients is pointwise; real coefficients in scalar actions are explicitly cast to ℂ.
