argument.text: H001-H003 give the ranges T>0, 0<gamma<=1, R>0. Fix arbitrary real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma and assume L1: ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R. Let u0_m=P_(<=m)u0. The data are real mean-zero Fourier polynomials, ||u0_m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and ||u0_m-u0||_2 tends to zero by the convergent Fourier norm sum. N001 supplies exact solutions u_m,u with a common M bound and sup_[0,T]||u_m-u||_2<=C(T,2R)||u0_m-u0||_2 tending to zero. The solution u has precisely the continuous distributional smooth-approximation convention in the target.

produces.statement: The real mean-zero polynomial approximants u0_m have H^gamma norm <=R and their exact solutions converge uniformly in time in L2 to the specified u.

argument.text: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is continuous from mean-zero L2 to L2. Indeed N005 gives Dinv:L2->H^1 and the H^1 product bound; consequently F_tau:L2->H^1 is a continuous quadratic map. The first term of H_tau is a product of inverse derivatives. Its second has the continuous bilinear scalar mean P0(f^2) multiplied by S_tau Dinv f. Its third is the H^1 product (S_s Dinv f)^3 followed by Dinv. Its fourth is the product of D^(-2)F_tau(f) and Dinv f, with unitary S factors and a final D^(-2). Each is continuous into L2; all scalar coefficients, including tau^(-1), are finite for this fixed tau. Hence the map and all of its finitely many iterates are continuous. The same formulas preserve reality and zero mean: explicit P, outer inverse derivatives, and the zero-mean factor in the scalar-mean term show this directly.

produces.statement: For every fixed theta>0 and finite nonnegative msteps, Psi_theta and each of its first msteps iterates are continuous from mean-zero L2 to L2 and preserve reality and zero mean.

argument.text: Take C,tau0 from N011, determined only by T,gamma,R. Fix an arbitrary positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. Applying N011 to u0_m gives the same error bound C*tau^gamma for every m. By F002 the numerical iterates converge in L2 at each of the finitely many grid points, and F001 gives uniform convergence of the exact solutions. The reverse triangle inequality, followed by the maximum over L+1 points, passes the estimate to u0. Since C and tau0 depend only on T,gamma,R, their choice is uniform over the entire datum ball and all L, this is the full conclusion P, including n=0. The finite-step continuity argument uses fixed tau only and imposes no support restriction or numerical H^gamma bound. Discharge L1 into the stated datum-ball antecedent and universally quantify u0 and the allowed L.

value.fact: On the normalized torus Jf(x)=-f(-x) has Fourier coefficients -hat f(-k), is an involutive isometry on each H^s and mean-zero dot H^s, and preserves reality and mean zero. It acts on distributions by pullback. For the source PDE, u=JU satisfies u_t+u_xxx=u u_x, with datum J U0=q; the transformation is reversible.

grounds.reason: Periodic normalized domain.
Fourier transform and distributional extension.
Even-in-k Fourier weights.
Source flow and equation.
Displayed sign-reflection and derivative signs.
Conservative distributional meaning of the quadratic term and exact-solution relation.

value.justification: Substitution x↦-x in the periodic Fourier integral gives the coefficient formula; reindexing nonnegative norm sums gives isometry, extended by completion or duality. The chain rule gives u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x, u_xxx=U_xxx. The same equalities hold distributionally by change of variable in test functions, with the locally integrable square transformed by reflection. Applying J twice is the identity, so solution correspondence and uniqueness are preserved.

value.fact: The multiplier S_t with symbol exp(i t k^3) is a strongly continuous isometry group on every H^s and mean-zero dot H^s. For a spatially smooth solution path of the target equation, v=S_{-t}u satisfies v'=S_{-t} partial_x(u^2)/2=B_t(v,v)/2, and ||v(t)||_H^gamma=||u(t)||_H^gamma.

grounds.reason: Explicit Fourier multiplier.
Definition of B_t.
Target PDE and smooth-data case established from source flow.

value.justification: The symbol has modulus one and obeys the group law. Strong continuity follows first on finite Fourier sums and then by their norm density and isometry. On smooth paths, termwise differentiation in any fixed lower Sobolev norm is justified by rapid Fourier decay; (S_{-t})'=partial_x^3 S_{-t}. Hence v'=S_{-t}(u_t+u_xxx)=S_{-t}partial_x(u^2)/2. The multiplier preserves every stated norm, including differences.

value.fact: For real mean-zero q in H^gamma, its symmetric Fourier truncations q_n are smooth, real, mean zero, converge in H^gamma, and satisfy ||q_n||_H^gamma<=||q||_H^gamma. E001's Lipschitz dependence gives convergence of their source flows in the continuous H^gamma solution class. A common H^gamma bound passes to a limit whenever every fixed-time Fourier coefficient converges; it holds at all times for a continuous representative even if first obtained almost everywhere.

grounds.reason: Reality and mean-zero coefficient conditions.
Summable norm and frequency truncations.
gamma>0.
Continuous source solution, dependence and a priori bound.
Datum ball and source estimate.
Smooth-approximation and finite-sum limit argument.
The required exact-solution convention is precisely smooth approximation of this same conservative equation.

value.justification: Truncation removes a nonnegative norm tail tending to zero and respects conjugate symmetry. Apply the supplied continuous dependence to these data; norm isometry transfers convergence to target flows. For every finite frequency set F, coefficient convergence gives sum_F <k>^(2 gamma)|hat f(k)|^2<=A^2 from a common bound A. Taking the supremum over finite F gives the full bound. If the bound initially holds a.e., continuity of the H^gamma norm and density of a full-measure subset of [0,T] extend it to every time. This is a lower-semicontinuity argument, not an exchange of an uncontrolled infinite sum with a limit.

value.fact: A smooth periodic datum belongs to every integer Sobolev space. A flow continuous in H^n for every positive integer n is spatially smooth at every time; the source solutions obtained at the different integer exponents agree by E001 uniqueness. The target smooth flow then has enough time regularity to differentiate its twist in any fixed Sobolev space.

grounds.reason: Fourier representation on the torus.
Weighted ell2 Sobolev norms.
Existence and uniqueness for every positive exponent and source equation.
Integer-exponent applications for smooth q.

value.justification: Integration by parts gives arbitrarily fast Fourier coefficient decay for smooth data. Conversely, for each j choose an integer n>j+1/2; Cauchy–Schwarz bounds sum_k |k|^j |hat f(k)| by ||f||_H^n times the finite square root of sum_k <k>^(2j-2n). Thus the differentiated Fourier series converges uniformly, and f is C^j. The same estimate transfers time continuity from H^n to C^j. The PDE consequently has a continuous right side in each fixed Sobolev space (choose higher n for the three derivatives and the product). Integrating the distributional time equation gives C^1 time regularity there. These are routine regularity consequences of the supplied all-integer bounds, not an additional PDE existence theorem.

result.text:
1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 180 seconds, and use the controller-owned 20,000,000 heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.
51: 
52: Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its
53: worker parameters, instances and direct inputs. Explicitly supply parameters
54: that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is
55: not an inference rule. The strict declaration check defines the proposition,
56: without proving it, and rejects unresolved holes and non-proposition goals.
57: `#check` is a useful reader aid, not sufficient declaration acceptance. A proof
58: body cannot resolve a hole in its preceding theorem declaration.
59: 
60: Checked auxiliary propositions receive a `yui_aux_...` name and an explicit
61: application with the existing local parameters/inputs. Reuse these theorems in
62: later auxiliary checks and the final body. The controller retains their actual
63: proof bodies and compiles them into standalone assembly. They are same-node
64: implementation lemmas, not extra assumptions. Read the helper index after a
65: context reset; never rebuild a checked helper merely because a turn ended.
66: 
67: Separate diagnostic printing from proving. `show_term` and similar suggestion
68: output may spend substantial time after the proof tactic runs. If that diagnostic
69: wrapper is implicated, check the same proof without it; only the new successful
70: check establishes acceptance. Do not ignore an unsuccessful process exit. If
71: small helpers pass but a monolithic body exhausts resources, retain the separate
72: checked helper declarations and compose them rather than repeatedly copying
73: their bodies into a growing proof.

value.fact: For real lambda, f_lambda(s)=exp(-i*lambda*s) is smooth, |f_lambda(s)|=1 and f_lambda'(s)=-i*lambda*f_lambda(s). For continuous complex u on a compact interval, |integral u|<=integral |u|; for C1 complex u,v on [0,tau], u(s)-u(r)=integral_r^s u'(t)dt and integral_0^tau u*v'=[u*v]_0^tau-integral_0^tau u'*v. Consequently |f_lambda(s)-f_lambda(r)|<=|lambda|*|s-r|. If h=f_alpha-M_tau(f_alpha) and beta!=0, then |M_tau(h*f_beta)|<=(|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral_0^tau|h'|)/(tau*|beta|), and integral_0^tau|h'|=tau*|alpha|.

grounds.reason: Provides the normalized integrals and the exponential functions.
Fixes tau>0 and real phases, defines h, and restricts integration by parts to the nonzero-phase branch.

value.justification: The exponential derivative and modulus follow from exp(ix)=cos(x)+i sin(x) for real x. FTC and integration by parts apply to real and imaginary components of these C1 functions. The integral norm inequality follows by projecting the complex integral onto its unit direction and bounding each real projection by |u| (the zero integral is immediate). Applying FTC and this inequality gives the Lipschitz bound. In integration by parts take u=h and v=f_beta/(-i*beta); its modulus is 1/|beta|. The displayed estimate follows by the triangle inequality, and subtracting a constant average leaves |h'|=|alpha|. These are routine calculus applications to the supplied smooth formulas, without a limiting interchange.

value.fact: For the h in S001 and s in [0,tau], |h(s)|<=tau^(-1)*integral_0^tau |alpha|*|s-r|dr<=tau*|alpha|. At the endpoints the sharper bounds are |h(0)|<=tau*|alpha|/2 and |h(tau)|<=tau*|alpha|/2, hence their sum is at most tau*|alpha|.

grounds.reason: Defines h with tau>0 and establishes |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha|*|s-r|.
M_tau is the normalized integral over [0,tau].

value.justification: Linearity gives h(s)=tau^(-1)*integral_0^tau(f_alpha(s)-f_alpha(r))dr. Apply the integral norm bound and the Lipschitz inequality. The rough estimate uses |s-r|<=tau. At s=0 and s=tau the integrals of |s-r| are each tau^2/2; division by positive tau yields the endpoint bounds. This expands the stated averaging step and verifies its constant without changing the route.

value.fact: For finite real sequences u,v, |sum_i u_i v_i| <= (sum_i u_i^2)^(1/2)(sum_i v_i^2)^(1/2). Restricting indices or composing one sequence with an injective index map bounds the resulting sum of nonnegative products by the product of the original ell2 norms. In particular sum_{i in E} u_i <= sqrt(|E|) (sum_{i in E}u_i^2)^(1/2) for nonnegative u.

grounds.reason: The initial inputs are finitely supported; fixing the two smaller frequencies determines one large frequency from the other by an injective translated reflection. Each smaller shell is finite.

value.justification: If sum v_i^2>0, expanding sum_i(u_i-t v_i)^2>=0 at t=(sum_i u_i v_i)/(sum_i v_i^2) proves the squared inequality; if the denominator vanishes all v_i vanish. Taking nonnegative square roots proves the claim. A restriction or injective reindexing uses only a subset of the nonnegative squares. Taking v_i=1 on E gives the cardinality bound.

value.fact: For rho=2^(-1/2) in (0,1), sum_{r>=0}rho^r=1/(1-rho). Consequently, for finitely supported nonnegative shell arrays U,V, sum_{ell>=m>=0}rho^(ell-m)U_ell V_m <= ||U||_ell2 ||V||_ell2/(1-rho).

grounds.reason: The shell norms are nonnegative and finitely supported for the initial finite-input estimate.
The displayed kernel is exactly rho^(ell-m); setting r=ell-m gives shifted scalar products, each bounded by BG001.

value.justification: For each r>=0, sum_{m>=0}U_(m+r)V_m <= ||U||_ell2||V||_ell2 by finite Cauchy–Schwarz and restriction of the square sum. Summing with weights rho^r gives the bound. The finite geometric identity sum_{r=0}^L rho^r=(1-rho^(L+1))/(1-rho), with rho^(L+1) tending to zero for 0<rho<1, gives the stated sum.

value.fact: For a nonnegative family (a_i) on a countable set I, define its sum as the supremum of finite subsums. If finite E_m increase and exhaust I, then sum_I a_i=sup_m sum_{E_m}a_i. Such sums are monotone under restricting indices and can be regrouped along a countable partition. In particular the shell square norms satisfy sum_j X_(r,j)^2=||x_r||_ell2^2, and common frequency cutoffs exhaust the quartic sum.

grounds.reason: The frequencies are nonzero integers, the denominator is bounded below by 2^j3, and the dyadic shells form a disjoint partition of those integers.

This paragraph explicitly passes to arbitrary nonnegative square-summable inputs. Its cutoff sets consist of zero-sum nonzero quadruples with every |k|<=m; they are finite, nested and exhaust the full index set. The finite estimate has a uniform constant.

value.justification: Every finite subset of I lies in some E_m, giving both inequalities between the two suprema. Monotonicity follows by inclusion of finite subsets. For a partition, each finite subsum meets finitely many parts, while finite approximations within finitely many parts give the reverse regrouping inequality. Apply this to the squares and then to the nonnegative quartic summands. Truncated square norms do not exceed the full square norms, so the uniform finite bound passes to the supremum without exchanging any signed sums.

value.fact: For positive U,V and 0<=s<=1, 0<=X<=U and X<=V imply X<=U^(1-s)V^s. Applied to X=|eta|/|k|, U=6/N3 and V=18 tau |abc|/N3, this gives the displayed F001 estimate, including s=0 and s=1.

grounds.reason: The two endpoint bounds are derived there from N002; surviving terms have |abc|>0, |k|>0 and N3>0, and tau>0.
The exponent satisfies 0<=s<=1.

Restricting the positive summation set can only decrease it.

Fix s in [0,1], tau>0, nonnegative n and mean-zero polynomial inputs f1,f2,f3. In each nonzero term of R2 put d=-k, p=a+b, A=|ab|, B0=|cd| and order the four magnitudes. The phase ratios are A/B0 and B0/A. N002 yields |eta|/|k|<=6/N3. Its small-time bound also gives |eta|/(tau|abck|)<=3|p|*min(A,B0)/(A B0)=3|p|/max(A,B0)<=18/N3. The geometric mean with weights 1-s and s is |eta|/(|k|*|abc|^s)<=6^(1-s)*18^s*tau^s/N3. Terms with zero phase or input, or with zero output, contribute zero, so no division by zero is used.

Dualize the R2 formula against an arbitrary ell2 coefficient sequence of norm one, take absolute values and use F001. Apply N003 with the first three sequences |a|^s|hat f1(a)|, |b|^s|hat f2(b)|, |c|^s|hat f3(c)| and the fourth the reflected absolute dual coefficients. Their norms are at most the H^s input norms and one. The prefactor tau/18 gives the asserted tau^(1+s) bound. The time phase and any inserted multiplier of modulus <=1 cannot increase this majorant. This includes each resonant restriction. Trilinearity and the estimate make polynomial approximations Cauchy in L2 and make the limit independent of approximating sequences; this gives the unique bounded trilinear extension.

Now H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Fix mean-zero w in H^gamma and f in L2, and temporarily assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1. F002 with sigma=gamma controls R2(w,w,w) by C M^3 tau^(1+gamma). Telescope R2(f,f,f)-R2(w,w,w) into three trilinear terms with one slot f-w and other slots chosen from f,w. F002 with sigma=0 controls their sum by C tau delta (||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Since ||f||_2<=M+1, this is at most C_M tau delta, proving the numerical-state estimate. The argument introduces no Sobolev regularity for f. Discharge L1 into the numerical-state bound's antecedent.

Orthogonality of exp(i*k*x) in normalized measure gives the L2 Fourier norm identity on polynomials; completion gives it on L2. Unimodularity and conjugate symmetry of exp(i*t*k^3) give unitarity, reality and mean preservation of S directly in Fourier coefficients. Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||Dinv f||_infty<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2, and ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. More generally H^1 embeds in L^infty by the same summable reciprocal weights. For A0,B0 in H^1, the product rule together with this embedding gives ||A0 B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1), first on polynomials and then by density. Apply this to the two inverse derivatives to obtain the J bound. The Fourier coefficient of a product of two L2 functions is bounded by the product of their L2 norms by Cauchy-Schwarz. Therefore ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-p_star))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0) k^2<k>^(-2*p_star), and this series converges because p_star=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum k^(-2) gives ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. On mean-zero coefficients <k>^(-p_star)<=|k|^(-1), so the negative-norm comparison follows. In J_t(A0,B0), bound its first inverse derivative in L2 and its second in L^infty to get the asymmetric bound. All constants are uniform in t since S is an isometry. Bounded-product extensions follow by the displayed estimates and density.

For smooth mean-zero paths f,g the nonzero kth Fourier coefficient of J_t(f,g) is sum_(a+b=k) exp(-i*3*k*a*b*t)(i*a)^(-1)(i*b)^(-1) hat f(a)hat g(b). Differentiating the phase contributes 3*i*k times the product coefficient. Thus partial_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Integrate in time and divide by three to obtain the normal-form identity with both endpoints. Smooth spatial Fourier series and their derivatives converge absolutely, justifying the differentiation. J is symmetric. In J_t(B_t(f,g),h), Dinv B_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t g)], since Dinv*partial_x=P. Substitution, without commuting any operator through a product, gives the stated Cint identity after integration. The calculation holds on each smooth time piece, so summing preserves both external endpoints. For time-independent f set g=f and divide the integral by two; this yields Stage(t;f)=[J_s(f,f)]/6.

Apply E002 with alpha=0 to arbitrary X paths on I=[a,b], 0<=a<=b, |I|<=1. This is exactly its L^infty L2 and derivative H^(-23/14) hypothesis, and any slot may carry the negative norm. For constant H^s inputs apply its time-independent clause with alpha=s in [0,1]. The source operator C is exactly Cint: e^(t partial_x^3)=S_(-t) and Fourier coefficients, projections and inverse derivatives agree. Every source L2 and H^r norm, and hence X norm, equals sqrt(2*pi) times ours. Dividing the trilinear inequalities by sqrt(2*pi) changes only their constants by 2*pi. Thus both normalized inequalities follow, also for continuous piecewise smooth paths with their weak derivatives.

H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Apply E003 with sigma=gamma, using epsilon=1/8 at gamma=1/2. Its a(sigma) equals a_gamma; all three cases give 0<=a_gamma<1. This gives ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^a_gamma). The bilinear conversion of source norms only changes the constant by sqrt(2*pi).

Choose once and for all 0<epsilon_stage<=1/8 sufficiently small for E004 at sigma=1/2. This choice follows from E004's 'any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0': the allowed positive epsilons include an interval immediately to the right of zero, which contains a number at most 1/8. Fix this choice independently of the state, norm bound, timestep, step index and spectral support. This auxiliary choice leaves a_gamma=1/8 at gamma=1/2 unchanged. Fix mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, 0<tau<=1 and n>=0. Apply E004 with f=g=w, sigma=gamma, beta=a_gamma, and epsilon=epsilon_stage in the midpoint case, uniformly over all times in the step. If 0<gamma<1/2, beta0=2*gamma-3/2, a_gamma-beta0=2-3*gamma>0 and 1+gamma-a_gamma=1/2+2*gamma>0. Its time exponent is (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma); subtracting gamma gives (gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2)/(5/2-gamma)>0, since the numerator equals (gamma-1/4)^2+7/16. If gamma=1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon_stage<1/8=a_gamma<3/2=1+gamma. The time exponent is (11/8)/(2+epsilon_stage)=11/(16+8*epsilon_stage)>=11/17>1/2=gamma. If 1/2<gamma<=1, beta0=gamma-1<=0=a_gamma<=1+gamma, and the time exponent (1+gamma)/2 is at least gamma. All denominators are positive. Thus in every case the allowed beta yields a power at least gamma. Because 0<tau<=1, replacing that power by gamma enlarges the right side, proving sup_step||Stage(t;w)||_(H^a_gamma)<=C_gamma*M^2*tau^gamma after converting norms. Next apply E004 with the same inputs and beta=1+gamma, retaining epsilon=epsilon_stage at the midpoint. This beta is the included upper endpoint; the denominator is respectively 5/2-gamma, 2+epsilon_stage, or 2, and the numerator is zero. Hence sup_step||Stage(t;w)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma*M^2. For either application, dividing the source output norm by sqrt(2*pi) and replacing the two source input norms by sqrt(2*pi) times their normalized norms only changes the constant by sqrt(2*pi). The fixed admissible midpoint choice is absorbed into C_gamma. Both constants therefore have the asserted C_(M,gamma) form and are independent of the step, interval position and spectral support. The arbitrary choices establish the two universal stage bounds, using only the H^gamma regularity of w.

Fix a smooth real mean-zero initial datum and tau>0. All products and Fourier multipliers preserve smoothness and reality. F_tau has P in both terms. H_tau has P in its first term, its second is a scalar mean times S_tau Dinv f, and both endpoint terms have an outer inverse derivative. Thus every iterate stays smooth real and mean zero. At each step take f=S_(-t_n)u^n. Apply E005: v^(n+1)=f+F_n(t_n+tau)+C_n(t_n+tau)-R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f). Here source e^(t partial_x^3)=S_(-t), source A^n=C_n(t_n+tau), and source R2 is D012 with the identical -tau/(18*i*k), covariance and phases. The source physical step agrees term by term with D008-D009, including S_(s-tau) in the last endpoint product.

The Interp formula gives V_n(t_n)=f. At the other endpoint Q_n cancels its part of W_n, leaving F001, so V_n(t_n+tau)=v^(n+1). Thus V is continuous and piecewise smooth and Y_n(t_n)=0. Differentiate the formula: V_n'=B_t(f+F_n,f+F_n)/2-W_n/tau=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau. Expanding V_n=z_n+Y_n by bilinearity gives V_n'-B_t(V_n,V_n)/2=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau=rho_n'. Concatenating these increments gives the asserted equation and Rres(0)=0.

Fix M>=1, smooth mean-zero f,w and 0<tau<=1, n>=0; assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M and delta=||f-w||_2<=1. Put q=tau^gamma+delta<=2. N005 gives F_n(t)=[J_s(f,f)]/6 and hence sup||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M and sup||F_n-Stage(t;w)||_(H^1)<=C_M delta, by bilinearity and ||f||_2<=M+1. N006 and a_gamma<1 then give ||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2<=C_M q. Since z_n'=B_t(f,f)/2, N005 also gives ||z_n||_X<=C_M.

Set A0=Stage(t;w) and D0=F_n-A0. The exact-data square satisfies ||partial_x[(S_t A0)^2]||_2<=2 C_gamma ||A0||_(H^(1+gamma))||A0||_(H^a_gamma)<=C_M tau^gamma, by N006 and the product rule. The difference of squares is (S_t D0) S_t(F_n+A0). Its derivative is bounded in L2 by the H^1 algebra bound of N005 and F001, giving C_M delta. Thus sup||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M q and sup||Q_n||_2<=C_M tau q. Apply the numerical-state clause of N004 to f,w to control R2(f,f,f) by C_M tau q. Therefore ||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q.

Use Dinv B_t(f,F_n)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F_n)]. Split f=w+(f-w). N006 bounds the w-product by C_gamma||w||_(H^gamma)||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)<=C_M q; the other product is <=delta||S_t F_n||_infty<=C_M delta by F001 and N005's H^1 embedding. Hence ||Dinv B_t(f,F_n)||_2<=C_M q. Differentiation gives Y_n'=B_t(f,F_n)+B_t(F_n,F_n)/2-W_n/tau. F002 and boundedness of Dinv on mean-zero L2 yield ||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M q. Integrating from Y_n(t_n)=0 gives ||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q.

Apply N005's normal form to C_n with f constant and F_n'=B_t(f,f)/2. As F_n(t_n)=0, C_n(t)=J_t(f,F_n(t))/3-Cint_[t_n,t](f,f,f)/6. The first term is O(q) by F001 and N005. In the cubic integral telescope f around w. N006 with exponent gamma on (w,w,w) gives O(tau^gamma) and with exponent zero on the three difference terms gives O(delta). Therefore ||C_n||_2<=C_M q. F002 and Y_n=C_n+Q_n-(t-t_n)W_n/tau now give ||Y_n||_2<=C_M q. From F003 and the mean-zero comparison ||Y_n||_(H^(-p_star))<=||Dinv Y_n||_2, also applied to Y_n', obtain ||Y_n||_X<=C_M q and ||Y_n||_(H^(-p_star))<=C_M tau q. All output clauses hold under L1. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the data.

Fix arbitrary step data M,f,w,tau,n and assume L1: M>=1, 0<tau<=1, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M and delta=||f-w||_2<=1. Set q=tau^gamma+delta. Apply N008 to this same Interp tuple. In the first integral of rho_n apply N005's normal form to (Y_n,z_n). The boundary is O(tau q) by ||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q, ||z_n||_2<=C_M and the asymmetric J bound. The integral with Y_n' is O(tau q) by ||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M q. In the remaining term z_n'=B_t(f,f)/2, symmetry of J and N005's cubic identity give a constant multiple of Cint(f,f,Y_n). By N006 with the negative norm on Y_n its bound is C tau||f||_X^2||Y_n||_X+C||f||_2^2||Y_n||_(L^infty H^(-p_star))<=C_M tau q; f is constant so ||f||_X=||f||_2<=M+1.

For the second integral apply N005's normal form to (Y_n,Y_n). Its boundary is <=C||Dinv Y_n||_2||Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q^2, and its differentiated terms have integrals <=C tau||Dinv Y_n'||_2||Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q^2. Since q<=2 this is O(tau q). The affine W_n term is O(tau q) by N008. Thus sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M tau q. Directly in Rres'=-B(Y_n,z_n)-B(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau, apply N005's negative-norm product bound and N008's strong bounds and W_n bound, giving ||Rres'||_(L^infty H^(-p_star))<=C_M(q+q^2)<=C_M q. Both output inequalities hold under L1; discharge L1.

Fix any smooth real mean-zero solution u of u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on [0,T], the normalized KdV equation of D020, and define v(t)=S_(-t)u(t). Take its numerical interpolation V with residual Rres. Put M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma), e=v-V and fix I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, 0<tau<=1. Assume L1: E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1. At each step intersecting I use f=v^n=V(t_n), w=v(t_n), delta_n=||f-w||_2<=E_I and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. N007 supplies the actual residual identity and grid values, and N009 gives sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n and ||Rres'||_(L^infty H^(-p_star))<=C_M q_n. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps (including a final partial step). Hence sup_(a<=t<=b)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_M(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). For the exact path, D004 gives partial_t S_(-t)=partial_x^3 S_(-t), commuting with spatial derivatives. Thus v'=S_(-t)(u_t+u_xxx)=(1/2)S_(-t)partial_x(u^2)=(1/2)B_t(v,v), since S_t v=u. Smoothness justifies this differentiation and the spatial products. Subtracting N007's identity V'=B_t(V,V)/2+Rres' and using symmetry and bilinearity gives e'=(B_t(v,v)-B_t(V,V))/2-Rres'=B_t(e,(v+V)/2)-Rres'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 then gives ||e||_X(I)<=C_M(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_X(I)+||V||_X(I)<=C_M. Here V=v-e, and the exact solution has L2 norm <=M throughout.

Define FI(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds. Integration gives e(t)=e(a)+FI(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Fix N>=2 only for analysis. For low frequencies N005's bound ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2, followed by two powers of frequency on |k|<=N, gives sup_I||P_(<=N)FI||_2<=C_M N^2 h E_I. For high frequencies apply the normal form in N005 with g=v-e/2, retaining both endpoints. Since e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=B(v,v)/2-B(e,g)/2+Rres'/2, symmetry of J and the cubic identity give exactly FI(t)=[J_s(e,g)]_a^t/3-Cint_[a,t](e,g,V)/3-Cint_[a,t](v,v,e)/6+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Indeed g-e/2=V combines the first differentiated pair, and -J(Rres',g)+J(e,Rres')/2=-J(Rres',V) before multiplication by -1/3. N005's H^1 bound on J bounds both high-output endpoints by C_M N^(-1)E_I. This includes the initial endpoint when e(a)!=0.

Let f1,f2,f3 be any three paths of finite X norm on I. For each path decompose frequencies at N/3. If all three input frequencies have modulus <=N/3, their sum has modulus <=N, so that cubic contribution vanishes after P_(>N). Multilinearity writes the remaining contribution as the sum of Cint(P_(>N/3)f1,f2,f3), Cint(P_(<=N/3)f1,P_(>N/3)f2,f3), and Cint(P_(<=N/3)f1,P_(<=N/3)f2,P_(>N/3)f3). Fourier projections contract L2 and the derivative H^(-23/14) norm. Each designated high input has H^(-23/14) norm <=C N^(-23/14) times its L2 norm. N006 therefore bounds this sum by C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-23/14)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infty L2), putting the negative norm on the designated high input in each summand. Instantiate this inequality for (e,g,V) and (v,v,e), where g=v-e/2. F001 gives ||e||_X<=C_M(tau^gamma+E_I), the other X norms <=C_M, and their L2 products <=C_M E_I. Consequently the two projected cubic integrals have total norm <=C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-23/14))*E_I.

For the forcing term in F002 use the actual stepwise Rres' from N007. On each intersected step define again f=v^n, w=v(t_n), delta_n=||f-w||_2 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. On this step the forcing integral is the sum -Cint(Y_n,z_n,V)-Cint(Y_n,Y_n,V)/2-tau^(-1)integral J_s(W_n,V)ds over that intersection. N008 gives ||Y_n||_X<=C_M q_n and ||Y_n||_(L^infty H^(-p_star))<=C_M tau q_n. N006 with the negative norm on Y_n, and F001's bound on V, control each cubic term by C_M tau q_n; for the term with two Y_n use q_n<=2. N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n and N005's L2 bound for J control the last integral by C_M tau q_n, even on a partial step. Summing yields C_M(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). Together with F002-F003 this gives sup||P_(>N)FI||_2<=C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-p_star))E_I. Add the low-frequency estimate and F001's residual bound in the exact error identity. The result is E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-23/14))*E_I. Discharge L1.

Fix a smooth real mean-zero datum u0 and assume L1: ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R. H001-H003 and N001 give a common M bound depending only on T,gamma,R. Take the exact u from N001, put v=S_(-t)u, construct V by Interp, and set e=v-V. N001 identifies u as a smooth solution of u_t+u_xxx=u*u_x=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) and v=S_(-t)u, so the explicit normalized exact-solution premise of N010 is satisfied. Use N010 with a constant C_M enlarged to work throughout this ball. Define N=ceil(max(2,8*C_M,(8*C_M)^(14/23))). Then C_M(N^(-1)+N^(-23/14))<=1/4. Then choose delta in (0,1] so small that C_M delta(N^2+3)<=1/4, and restrict tau<=delta/2. On any interval starting at a grid point and of length h<=delta with error supremum <=1, N010 absorbs the error coefficient: h+tau<=3delta/2, and hence E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+C'_M delta*tau^gamma. These choices depend only on the common M and gamma,T.

Partition the grid into blocks of floor(delta/tau) steps and a possibly shorter final block. Full block lengths belong to [delta/2,delta], so there are at most 2T/delta+1 blocks. Iterate F001, beginning with e(0)=0, to get sup_[0,t]||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma on every prefix on which ||e||_2<=1; K depends only on T,gamma,R. This includes a prefix ending inside the last step, because N010 explicitly allows a partial final interval. N007 gives continuity of the interpolant; the exact solution is continuous by N001. For contradiction assume L2: the error first reaches one at a time in [0,T]. At that first time, the same finite recurrence through that first time would give <=K*tau^gamma. Choose tau0<=min(1,delta/2) so small that K*tau0^gamma<1/2, possible because H002 gives gamma>0. This contradicts L2, which is discharged; hence the estimate holds on all [0,T]. N007 gives V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)u^n and N001 gives unitarity of the twist, so the grid-point bound follows. No bound depends on higher smooth norms or spectral support. Discharge L1 into the datum-ball antecedent and quantify over all such smooth data.

H001-H003 give the ranges T>0, 0<gamma<=1, R>0. Fix arbitrary real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma and assume L1: ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R. Let u0_m=P_(<=m)u0. The data are real mean-zero Fourier polynomials, ||u0_m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and ||u0_m-u0||_2 tends to zero by the convergent Fourier norm sum. N001 supplies exact solutions u_m,u with a common M bound and sup_[0,T]||u_m-u||_2<=C(T,2R)||u0_m-u0||_2 tending to zero. The solution u has precisely the continuous distributional smooth-approximation convention in the target.

For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is continuous from mean-zero L2 to L2. Indeed N005 gives Dinv:L2->H^1 and the H^1 product bound; consequently F_tau:L2->H^1 is a continuous quadratic map. The first term of H_tau is a product of inverse derivatives. Its second has the continuous bilinear scalar mean P0(f^2) multiplied by S_tau Dinv f. Its third is the H^1 product (S_s Dinv f)^3 followed by Dinv. Its fourth is the product of D^(-2)F_tau(f) and Dinv f, with unitary S factors and a final D^(-2). Each is continuous into L2; all scalar coefficients, including tau^(-1), are finite for this fixed tau. Hence the map and all of its finitely many iterates are continuous. The same formulas preserve reality and zero mean: explicit P, outer inverse derivatives, and the zero-mean factor in the scalar-mean term show this directly.

Take C,tau0 from N011, determined only by T,gamma,R. Fix an arbitrary positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. Applying N011 to u0_m gives the same error bound C*tau^gamma for every m. By F002 the numerical iterates converge in L2 at each of the finitely many grid points, and F001 gives uniform convergence of the exact solutions. The reverse triangle inequality, followed by the maximum over L+1 points, passes the estimate to u0. Since C and tau0 depend only on T,gamma,R, their choice is uniform over the entire datum ball and all L, this is the full conclusion P, including n=0. The finite-step continuity argument uses fixed tau only and imposes no support restriction or numerical H^gamma bound. Discharge L1 into the stated datum-ball antecedent and universally quantify u0 and the allowed L.

import Mathlib
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal
open MeasureTheory Filter Set
noncomputable section
namespace KdV
abbrev Coeff := ℤ → ℂ
abbrev Curve := ℝ → Coeff
def weight (s : ℝ) (k : ℤ) : ℝ := (1 + (k : ℝ)^2) ^ s
def H (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Prop := Summable (fun k => weight s k * ‖f k‖^2)
def hn (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (∑' k, weight s k * ‖f k‖^2)
def dh (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Prop :=
  f 0 = 0 ∧ Summable (fun k : ℤ => if k = 0 then 0 else |(k : ℝ)|^(2*s) * ‖f k‖^2)
def dn (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (∑' k : ℤ, if k = 0 then 0 else |(k : ℝ)|^(2*s) * ‖f k‖^2)
def realCoeff (f : Coeff) : Prop := ∀ k, f (-k) = star (f k)
def mz (f : Coeff) : Prop := f 0 = 0
def data (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Prop := H s f ∧ mz f
def rd (s : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Prop := data s f ∧ realCoeff f
def smooth (f : Coeff) : Prop := ∀ m : ℕ, H (m : ℝ) f
def poly (f : Coeff) : Prop := Set.Finite (Function.support f)
def ik (k : ℤ) : ℂ := Complex.I * (k : ℂ)
def air (t : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  fun k => Complex.exp (Complex.I * (t : ℂ) * (k : ℂ)^3) * f k
def proj (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => if k = 0 then 0 else f k
def mean (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => if k = 0 then f 0 else 0
def invD (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => if k = 0 then 0 else (ik k)⁻¹ * f k
def invD2 (f : Coeff) : Coeff := invD (invD f)
def dx (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => ik k * f k
def mul (f g : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => ∑' a : ℤ, f a * g (k-a)
def cube (f : Coeff) : Coeff := mul (mul f f) f
def low (N : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff := fun k => if |(k : ℝ)| ≤ N then f k else 0
def high (N : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff := f - low N f
def eval (f : Coeff) (x : ℝ) : ℂ := ∑' k : ℤ, Complex.exp (Complex.I * (k : ℂ) * (x : ℂ)) * f k
def linfty (f : Coeff) : ℝ := sSup ((fun x => ‖eval f x‖) '' Icc 0 (2*Real.pi))
def bn (t : ℝ) (f g : Coeff) : Coeff := air (-t) (dx (mul (air t f) (air t g)))
def jn (t : ℝ) (f g : Coeff) : Coeff := air (-t) (proj (mul (air t (invD f)) (air t (invD g))))
def cint (a b : ℝ) (f g h : Curve) : Coeff :=
  fun k => ∫ t in a..b, (air (-t) (proj (mul (proj (mul (air t (f t)) (air t (g t)))) (air t (invD (h t)))))) k
def intC (a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : Coeff := fun k => ∫ t in a..b, f t k
def stage (n : ℕ) (τ t : ℝ) (f g : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  (1/2 : ℂ) • intC ((n : ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r f g)
def favg (τ α : ℝ) : ℂ := (τ : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..τ, Complex.exp (-Complex.I * (t : ℂ) * (α : ℂ))
def eta (τ α β : ℝ) : ℂ := favg τ (α+β) - favg τ α * favg τ β
def phase1 (a b : ℤ) : ℝ := 3*(a:ℝ)*(b:ℝ)*((a+b):ℤ)
def phase2 (k c p : ℤ) : ℝ := 3*(k:ℝ)*(c:ℝ)*(p:ℝ)
abbrev Mult := ℤ → ℤ → ℤ → ℤ → ℂ
def unitMult : Mult := fun _ _ _ _ => 1
def rterm (μ : Mult) (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f g h : Coeff) (k : ℤ) (v : ℤ × ℤ) : ℂ :=
  let a := v.1
  let b := v.2
  let c := k-a-b
  let α := phase1 a b
  let β := phase2 k c (a+b)
  if k = 0 ∨ a+b = 0 then 0 else
    -(τ : ℂ)/(18*ik k) * μ k a b c *
      Complex.exp (-Complex.I * ((n:ℝ)*τ : ℝ) * ((α+β : ℝ) : ℂ)) *
      eta τ α β * f a * g b * h c
def rem (μ : Mult) (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f g h : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  fun k => ∑' v : ℤ × ℤ, rterm μ n τ f g h k v
def quad (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  (1/6 : ℂ) • proj (mul (air τ (invD f)) (air τ (invD f))) -
  (1/6 : ℂ) • air τ (proj (mul (invD f) (invD f)))
def cubic (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  let F := quad τ f
  let E := fun s => air (τ-s) (invD (cube (air s (invD f))))
  let G := fun s => air (τ-s) (invD2 (mul (air (s-τ) (invD2 F)) (air s (invD f))))
  (1/3 : ℂ) • proj (mul (air τ (invD f)) (invD F)) +
  ((τ/9 : ℝ) : ℂ) • mul (air τ (invD f)) (mean (mul f f)) -
  (1/54 : ℂ) • (E τ - E 0) - ((1/(27*τ) : ℝ) : ℂ) • (G τ - G 0)
def step (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff := air τ f + quad τ f + cubic τ f
def iter (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : ℕ → Coeff
  | 0 => q
  | n+1 => step τ (iter τ q n)
def pstar : ℝ := 23/14
def aux (γ : ℝ) : ℝ := if γ < 1/2 then 1/2-γ else if γ = 1/2 then 1/8 else 0
def sourceAux (s ε : ℝ) : ℝ := if s = 0 then 1/2+ε else if s < 1/2 then 1/2-s else if s = 1/2 then ε else 0
def beta0 (s ε : ℝ) : ℝ := if s < 1/2 then 2*s-3/2 else if s = 1/2 then -1/2-ε else s-1
def k3 (a b c d : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  max (min |(a:ℝ)| (min |(b:ℝ)| |(c:ℝ)|))
    (max (min |(a:ℝ)| (min |(b:ℝ)| |(d:ℝ)|))
      (max (min |(a:ℝ)| (min |(c:ℝ)| |(d:ℝ)|)) (min |(b:ℝ)| (min |(c:ℝ)| |(d:ℝ)|))))
def contH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, H s (f t)) ∧
  ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧
    ∀ r ∈ Icc a b, |r-t| < δ → hn s (f r - f t) < ε
def convH (s : ℝ) (f : ℕ → Coeff) (g : Coeff) : Prop :=
  (∀ n, H s (f n)) ∧ H s g ∧ Tendsto (fun n => hn s (f n-g)) atTop (nhds 0)
def supH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : ℝ := sSup ((fun t => hn s (f t)) '' Icc a b)
def boundedH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, H s (f t)) ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, hn s (f t) ≤ C
def aeH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : ℤ, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun t => f t k) (volume.restrict (Icc a b))) ∧
  (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc a b)), H s (f t)) ∧
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc a b)), hn s (f t) ≤ C
def essH (s a b : ℝ) (f : Curve) : ℝ :=
  (essSup (fun t => ENNReal.ofReal (hn s (f t))) (volume.restrict (Icc a b))).toReal
def weakD (a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : ℤ, IntervalIntegrable (fun t => df t k) volume a b) ∧
  ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ∀ k : ℤ, f t k = f a k + ∫ r in a..t, df r k
def admissible (s a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : Prop :=
  aeH s a b f ∧ aeH (-pstar) a b df ∧ weakD a b f df
def xn (a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : ℝ := essH 0 a b f + essH (-pstar) a b df
def normDeriv (s a b t : ℝ) (f : Curve) (d : Coeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ r ∈ Icc a b,
    0 < |r-t| → |r-t| < δ →
      hn s (f r - f t - ((r-t : ℝ) : ℂ) • d) ≤ ε * |r-t|
def smoothPair (a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : Prop :=
  ∀ m : ℕ, contH (m:ℝ) a b f ∧ contH (m:ℝ) a b df ∧
    ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, normDeriv (m:ℝ) a b t f (df t)
def piecewise (a b : ℝ) (f df : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : ℕ, contH (m:ℝ) a b f) ∧
  ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ → ℝ, ∃ d : ℕ → Curve,
    r 0 = a ∧ r N = b ∧
    (∀ j < N, r j ≤ r (j+1) ∧ smoothPair (r j) (r (j+1)) f (d j) ∧
      (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc (r j) (r (j+1)))), df t = d j t))
def twisted (sign : ℝ) (u : Curve) : Curve := fun t => air (-sign*t) (u t)
def rhs (sign : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  fun k => Complex.I * (sign : ℂ) * (k : ℂ)^3 * f k + (1/2 : ℂ) * ik k * mul f f k
def solution (sign s A : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (u : Curve) : Prop :=
  contH s 0 A u ∧ u 0 = q ∧
  (∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, realCoeff (u t) ∧ mz (u t)) ∧
  (∀ k : ℤ, IntervalIntegrable (fun t => rhs sign (u t) k) volume 0 A) ∧
  ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, ∀ k : ℤ, u t k = q k + ∫ r in (0:ℝ)..t, rhs sign (u r) k
def smoothCurve (a b : ℝ) (u : Curve) : Prop := ∀ m : ℕ, contH (m:ℝ) a b u
def exact (sign s A : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (u : Curve) : Prop :=
  solution sign s A q u ∧ ∃ us : ℕ → Curve,
    (∀ m : ℕ, solution sign 0 A (low (m:ℝ) q) (us m) ∧ smoothCurve 0 A (us m)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun m => supH 0 0 A (fun t => us m t-u t)) atTop (nhds 0)
end KdV

namespace KdV
def srcScale : ℝ := Real.sqrt (2*Real.pi)
def pairing (f g : Coeff) : ℂ := ∑' k : ℤ, f k * star (g k)
def L1dual (s A : ℝ) (g : Curve) : Prop :=
  (∀ k : ℤ, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun t => g t k) (volume.restrict (Icc 0 A))) ∧
  (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume.restrict (Icc 0 A)), dh (-s) (g t)) ∧
  IntegrableOn (fun t => dn (-s) (g t)) (Icc 0 A) volume
def gal (A : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (m : ℕ) (u : Curve) : Prop :=
  u 0 = low (m:ℝ) q ∧ smoothCurve 0 A u ∧
  (∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, rd 0 (u t) ∧ low (m:ℝ) (u t) = u t) ∧
  weakD 0 A u (fun t => low (m:ℝ) (rhs (-1) (u t)))
def galBounds : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ B Q : ℝ, 0 ≤ B → 0 ≤ Q →
  ∃ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M ∧ ∀ q : Coeff, dh s q → realCoeff q → hn 0 q ≤ B → dn s q ≤ Q →
    ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ u : Curve, gal A q m u → ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, dn s (u t) ≤ M
def sourceCompactness : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ q : Coeff, dh s q → realCoeff q →
  ∀ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ < s →
  ∃ us : ℕ → Curve, ∃ u : Curve, ∃ κ : ℕ → ℕ,
    (∀ m, gal A q m (us m)) ∧ StrictMono κ ∧ exact (-1) s A q u ∧
    (∃ M : ℝ, (∀ m t, t ∈ Icc 0 A → dn s (us m t) ≤ M) ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, dn s (u t) ≤ M) ∧
    (∀ p : ℝ, 1 < p →
      Tendsto (fun j => ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..A, hn σ (us (κ j) t-u t)^p) atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
    (∀ g : Curve, L1dual s A g →
      Tendsto (fun j => ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..A, pairing (us (κ j) t) (g t)) atTop
        (nhds (∫ t in (0:ℝ)..A, pairing (u t) (g t))))
def sourceFlow : Prop :=
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ q : Coeff, dh s q → realCoeff q →
    ∃ u : Curve, exact (-1) s A q u ∧
      (∀ v : Curve, solution (-1) s A q v → EqOn u v (Icc 0 A)) ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, hn 0 (u t) = hn 0 q) ∧
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B →
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ q r : Coeff,
      dh s q → dh s r → realCoeff q → realCoeff r → dn s q + dn s r ≤ B →
      ∀ u v : Curve, exact (-1) s A q u → exact (-1) s A r v →
        ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, dn s (u t-v t) ≤ C*dn s (q-r)) ∧
  (∀ θ B : ℝ, -1 < θ → θ ≤ 0 → 0 ≤ B →
    ∃ C D : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < D ∧
      ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ q r : Coeff,
        rd 0 q → rd 0 r → hn 0 q+hn 0 r ≤ B →
        ∀ u v : Curve, exact (-1) 0 A q u → exact (-1) 0 A r v →
          ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A,
            dn θ (twisted (-1) u t-twisted (-1) v t) ≤ C*D^A*dn θ (q-r))
def sourceUniform : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ B Q : ℝ, 0 ≤ B → 0 ≤ Q →
  ∃ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M ∧ ∀ q : Coeff, dh s q → realCoeff q → hn 0 q ≤ B → dn s q ≤ Q →
    ∀ u : Curve, exact (-1) s A q u → ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 A, dn s (u t) ≤ M
def bit : Prop := galBounds ∧ sourceCompactness ∧ sourceFlow ∧ sourceUniform
def cubicBounds (K : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ α a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → b-a ≤ 1 →
    ∀ f df : Fin 3 → Curve, (∀ j, admissible α a b (f j) (df j)) →
      H 0 (cint a b (f 0) (f 1) (f 2)) ∧ ∀ i : Fin 3,
      K*hn 0 (cint a b (f 0) (f 1) (f 2)) ≤
        C*(b-a)*(∏ j : Fin 3, K*xn a b (f j) (df j)) +
        C*(K*essH (-pstar) a b (f i))*
          (∏ j ∈ (Finset.univ.erase i), K*essH 0 a b (f j))) ∧
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → b-a ≤ 1 →
    ∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, H s (f j)) →
      H 0 (cint a b (fun _ => f 0) (fun _ => f 1) (fun _ => f 2)) ∧
      K*hn 0 (cint a b (fun _ => f 0) (fun _ => f 1) (fun _ => f 2)) ≤
        C*(b-a)^s*(∏ j : Fin 3, K*hn s (f j)))
def productBounds (K : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 →
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ f g : Coeff, H s f → H (sourceAux s ε) g →
    H 0 (mul f g) ∧ K*hn 0 (mul f g) ≤ C*(K*hn s f)*(K*hn (sourceAux s ε) g)
def stageBoundAt (K s ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ β : ℝ, beta0 s ε ≤ β → β ≤ 1+s →
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ t : ℝ, 0 < τ →
  t ∈ Icc ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) →
  ∀ f g : Coeff, data s f → data s g →
    H β (stage n τ t f g) ∧
    K*hn β (stage n τ t f g) ≤
      C*τ^((1+s-β)/(1+s-beta0 s ε))*(K*hn s f)*(K*hn s g)
def stageBounds (K : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ 1 → s ≠ 1/2 → stageBoundAt K s 0) ∧
  ∃ ε0 : ℝ, 0 < ε0 ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < ε0 → stageBoundAt K (1/2) ε
def schemeIdentity : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → ∀ f : Coeff, smooth f → mz f →
    air (-((n:ℝ)*τ)-τ) (step τ (air ((n:ℝ)*τ) f)) =
      f + stage n τ (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) f f +
      intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) (fun t => bn t f (stage n τ t f f)) -
      rem unitMult n τ f f f
def fn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => stage n τ t f f
def zn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => f + fn n τ f t
def dz (f : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t f f
def cn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r f (fn n τ f r))
def qn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => (1/2 : ℂ) • intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r (fn n τ f r) (fn n τ f r))
def wn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Coeff :=
  qn n τ f (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) + rem unitMult n τ f f f
def vn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => f + fn n τ f t + cn n τ f t + qn n τ f t -
    (((t-(n:ℝ)*τ)/τ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
def yn (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve := vn n τ f - zn n τ f
def dy (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => bn t f (fn n τ f t) + (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (fn n τ f t) (fn n τ f t) -
    ((τ⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
def drho (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => -bn t (yn n τ f t) (zn n τ f t) -
    (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (yn n τ f t) (yn n τ f t) -
    ((τ⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
def rho (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f : Coeff) : Curve :=
  fun t => -intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r (yn n τ f r) (zn n τ f r)) -
    (1/2 : ℂ) • intC ((n:ℝ)*τ) t (fun r => bn r (yn n τ f r) (yn n τ f r)) -
    (((t-(n:ℝ)*τ)/τ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
def idx (τ t : ℝ) : ℕ := (Int.floor (t/τ)).toNat
def datum (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (n : ℕ) : Coeff := air (-((n:ℝ)*τ)) (iter τ q n)
def interp (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => vn (idx τ t) τ (datum τ q (idx τ t)) t
def residual (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : Curve := fun t =>
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (idx τ t), rho j τ (datum τ q j) (((j:ℝ)+1)*τ)) +
    rho (idx τ t) τ (datum τ q (idx τ t)) t
def dres (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : Curve := fun t => drho (idx τ t) τ (datum τ q (idx τ t)) t
def dvnum (τ : ℝ) (q : Coeff) : Curve := fun t =>
  let n := idx τ t
  let f := datum τ q n
  (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (zn n τ f t) (zn n τ f t) - ((τ⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • wn n τ f
end KdV

namespace KdV
def phaseEst : Prop :=
  ∀ τ α β : ℝ, 0 < τ →
    ((α = 0 ∨ β = 0) → eta τ α β = 0) ∧
    (α ≠ 0 → β ≠ 0 →
      ‖eta τ α β‖ ≤ 2*min |α/β| |β/α| ∧
      ‖eta τ α β‖ ≤ τ*min |α| |β|)
def freqEst : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c d : ℤ, a ≠ 0 → b ≠ 0 → c ≠ 0 → d ≠ 0 → a+b+c+d = 0 →
  ∀ N1 N2 N3 N4 : ℝ,
    List.Perm [|(a:ℝ)|, |(b:ℝ)|, |(c:ℝ)|, |(d:ℝ)|] [N1,N2,N3,N4] →
    N4 ≤ N3 → N3 ≤ N2 → N2 ≤ N1 →
    N1 ≤ 3*N2 ∧
    |(d:ℝ)|⁻¹ * min (|(a:ℝ)*(b:ℝ)|/|(c:ℝ)*(d:ℝ)|)
      (|(c:ℝ)*(d:ℝ)|/|(a:ℝ)*(b:ℝ)|) ≤ 3/N3 ∧
    |((a+b:ℤ):ℝ)| / max |(a:ℝ)*(b:ℝ)| |(c:ℝ)*(d:ℝ)| ≤ 6/N3
def phaseAndGeometry : Prop := phaseEst ∧ freqEst
def quadTerm (x : Fin 4 → ℤ → ℝ) (Ω : Set (ℤ × ℤ × ℤ)) (v : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ) : ℝ :=
  let a := v.1
  let b := v.2.1
  let c := v.2.2
  let d := -(a+b+c)
  @ite ℝ (v ∈ Ω ∧ a ≠ 0 ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ c ≠ 0 ∧ d ≠ 0)
    (Classical.propDecidable (v ∈ Ω ∧ a ≠ 0 ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ c ≠ 0 ∧ d ≠ 0))
    (x 0 a * x 1 b * x 2 c * x 3 d / k3 a b c d) 0
def fourLinear : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x : Fin 4 → ℤ → ℝ,
    (∀ j, x j 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ k, 0 ≤ x j k) ∧ Summable (fun k => (x j k)^2)) →
    ∀ Ω : Set (ℤ × ℤ × ℤ),
      Summable (quadTerm x Ω) ∧
      (∑' v, quadTerm x Ω v) ≤ C*(∏ j : Fin 4, Real.sqrt (∑' k, (x j k)^2))
def triOn (s : ℝ) (G : (Fin 3 → Coeff) → Coeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j)) → ∀ i : Fin 3,
    (∀ u v : Coeff, data s u → data s v →
      G (Function.update f i (u+v)) = G (Function.update f i u) + G (Function.update f i v)) ∧
    (∀ u : Coeff, data s u → ∀ c : ℂ,
      G (Function.update f i (c • u)) = c • G (Function.update f i u))
def triBound (s τ C : ℝ) (G : (Fin 3 → Coeff) → Coeff) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j)) →
    H 0 (G f) ∧ hn 0 (G f) ≤ C*τ^(1+s)*(∏ j : Fin 3, hn s (f j))
def remainderCore : Prop :=
  ∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ 1 → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
  ∀ μ : Mult, (∀ k a b c, ‖μ k a b c‖ ≤ 1) →
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ →
    let G := fun f : Fin 3 → Coeff => rem μ n τ (f 0) (f 1) (f 2)
    triOn s G ∧ triBound s τ C G ∧
    (∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j)) →
      ∀ k : ℤ, Summable (rterm μ n τ (f 0) (f 1) (f 2) k)) ∧
    (∀ F : (Fin 3 → Coeff) → Coeff, triOn s F →
      (∃ D : ℝ, 0 < D ∧ triBound s τ D F) →
      (∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j) ∧ poly (f j)) → F f = G f) →
      ∀ f : Fin 3 → Coeff, (∀ j, data s (f j)) → F f = G f)
def numericalRemainder (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → τ ≤ 1 →
  ∀ f w : Coeff, data 0 f → data γ w → hn γ w ≤ M → hn 0 (f-w) ≤ 1 →
    H 0 (rem unitMult n τ f f f) ∧
    hn 0 (rem unitMult n τ f f f) ≤ C*τ*(τ^γ+hn 0 (f-w))

def linearBounds : Prop :=
  (∀ s t : ℝ, ∀ f : Coeff, H s f → H s (air t f) ∧ hn s (air t f) = hn s f) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ f : Coeff, (realCoeff f → realCoeff (air t f)) ∧ (mz f → mz (air t f))) ∧
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    (∀ f : Coeff, data 0 f → H 1 (invD f) ∧ hn 1 (invD f)+linfty (invD f) ≤ C*hn 0 f) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ f g : Coeff, data 0 f → data 0 g →
      H (-pstar) (bn t f g) ∧ hn (-pstar) (bn t f g) ≤ C*hn 0 f*hn 0 g ∧
      H 1 (jn t f g) ∧ hn 1 (jn t f g) ≤ C*hn 0 f*hn 0 g) ∧
    (∀ f : Coeff, H 1 f → linfty f ≤ C*hn 1 f) ∧
    (∀ f g : Coeff, H 1 f → H 1 g →
      H 1 (mul f g) ∧ hn 1 (mul f g) ≤ C*hn 1 f*hn 1 g) ∧
    (∀ f g : Coeff, H 0 f → H 0 g →
      H 0 (invD (proj (mul f g))) ∧ hn 0 (invD (proj (mul f g))) ≤ C*hn 0 f*hn 0 g) ∧
    (∀ f : Coeff, mz f → H 0 (invD f) →
      H (-pstar) f ∧ hn (-pstar) f ≤ hn 0 (invD f)) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ f g : Coeff, mz f → H 0 (invD f) → H 0 g →
      H 0 (jn t f g) ∧ hn 0 (jn t f g) ≤ C*hn 0 (invD f)*hn 0 g)
def normalForms : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ f g : Coeff, data 0 f → data 0 g → jn t f g = jn t g f) ∧
  (∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → ∀ f df g dg : Curve,
    piecewise a b f df → piecewise a b g dg →
    (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, mz (f t) ∧ mz (g t)) →
    intC a b (fun t => bn t (f t) (g t)) =
      (1/3 : ℂ) • (jn b (f b) (g b)-jn a (f a) (g a)) -
      (1/3 : ℂ) • intC a b (fun t => jn t (df t) (g t)+jn t (f t) (dg t))) ∧
  (∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → ∀ f g h : Curve,
    smoothCurve a b f → smoothCurve a b g → smoothCurve a b h →
    (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, mz (f t) ∧ mz (g t) ∧ mz (h t)) →
    intC a b (fun t => jn t (bn t (f t) (g t)) (h t)) = cint a b f g h) ∧
  (∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ t : ℝ, 0 < τ →
    t ∈ Icc ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) → ∀ f : Coeff, data 0 f →
    stage n τ t f f = (1/6 : ℂ) • (jn t f f - jn ((n:ℝ)*τ) f f))
def basic : Prop := linearBounds ∧ normalForms
def normalizedProduct (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ f g : Coeff, H γ f → H (aux γ) g →
    H 0 (mul f g) ∧ hn 0 (mul f g) ≤ C*hn γ f*hn (aux γ) g
def normalizedStages (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
  ∀ w : Coeff, data γ w → hn γ w ≤ M → ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ t : ℝ, 0 < τ → τ ≤ 1 →
  t ∈ Icc ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ) →
    H (aux γ) (stage n τ t w w) ∧ hn (aux γ) (stage n τ t w w) ≤ C*τ^γ ∧
    H (1+γ) (stage n τ t w w) ∧ hn (1+γ) (stage n τ t w w) ≤ C
def continuousBounds (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  0 ≤ aux γ ∧ aux γ < 1 ∧ cubicBounds 1 ∧ normalizedProduct γ ∧ normalizedStages γ
def flow (T γ R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∃ A : ℝ, 0 ≤ A ∧ ∀ q : Coeff, rd γ q → hn γ q ≤ R →
    (∃ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u) ∧
    (∀ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u →
      (∀ v : Curve, solution 1 γ T q v → EqOn u v (Icc 0 T)) ∧
      (smooth q → smoothCurve 0 T u) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ Icc 0 T, hn γ (u t) ≤ A) ∧
      supH γ 0 T (twisted 1 u) ≤ A ∧
      (∀ s t : ℝ, t ∈ Icc 0 T → H s (u t) →
        H s (twisted 1 u t) ∧ hn s (twisted 1 u t) = hn s (u t)) ∧
      (smooth q → weakD 0 T (twisted 1 u)
        (fun t => (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (twisted 1 u t) (twisted 1 u t))))) ∧
  (∀ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ q r : Coeff,
    rd 0 q → rd 0 r → hn 0 q+hn 0 r ≤ B →
    ∀ u v : Curve, exact 1 0 T q u → exact 1 0 T r v →
      supH 0 0 T (u-v) ≤ C*hn 0 (q-r))
def interpolation : Prop :=
  ∀ q : Coeff, smooth q → realCoeff q → mz q → ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ →
    (∀ n : ℕ, smooth (iter τ q n) ∧ realCoeff (iter τ q n) ∧ mz (iter τ q n)) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, interp τ q ((n:ℝ)*τ) = datum τ q n) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, yn n τ (datum τ q n) ((n:ℝ)*τ) = 0) ∧
    (∀ L : ℕ, piecewise 0 ((L:ℝ)*τ) (interp τ q) (dvnum τ q) ∧
      weakD 0 ((L:ℝ)*τ) (interp τ q) (dvnum τ q) ∧
      weakD 0 ((L:ℝ)*τ) (residual τ q) (dres τ q)) ∧
    residual τ q 0 = 0 ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t →
      dvnum τ q t = (1/2 : ℂ) • bn t (interp τ q t) (interp τ q t) + dres τ q t) ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, ∀ t ∈ Icc ((n:ℝ)*τ) (((n:ℝ)+1)*τ),
      residual τ q t-residual τ q ((n:ℝ)*τ) = rho n τ (datum τ q n) t)
end KdV

def stepHyp (γ M τ : ℝ) (f w : Coeff) : Prop :=
  smooth f ∧ smooth w ∧ mz f ∧ mz w ∧ H γ w ∧ hn γ w ≤ M ∧ hn 0 (f-w) ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < τ ∧ τ ≤ 1
def stepControlsAt (γ C : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (f w : Coeff) : Prop :=
  let a := (n:ℝ)*τ
  let b := ((n:ℝ)+1)*τ
  let δ := hn 0 (f-w)
  let q := τ^γ+δ
  admissible 0 a b (zn n τ f) (dz f) ∧
  admissible 0 a b (yn n τ f) (dy n τ f) ∧
  xn a b (zn n τ f) (dz f) ≤ C ∧
  xn a b (yn n τ f) (dy n τ f) ≤ C*q ∧
  H 0 (wn n τ f) ∧ hn 0 (wn n τ f) ≤ C*τ*q ∧
  ∀ t ∈ Icc a b,
    H 1 (fn n τ f t) ∧ hn 1 (fn n τ f t) ≤ C ∧
    H 1 (fn n τ f t-stage n τ t w w) ∧ hn 1 (fn n τ f t-stage n τ t w w) ≤ C*δ ∧
    H (aux γ) (fn n τ f t) ∧ hn (aux γ) (fn n τ f t)+hn 0 (fn n τ f t) ≤ C*q ∧
    H 0 (bn t (fn n τ f t) (fn n τ f t)) ∧ hn 0 (bn t (fn n τ f t) (fn n τ f t)) ≤ C*q ∧
    H 0 (qn n τ f t) ∧ hn 0 (qn n τ f t)+hn 0 (wn n τ f) ≤ C*τ*q ∧
    H 0 (invD (yn n τ f t)) ∧ hn 0 (invD (yn n τ f t)) ≤ C*τ*q ∧
    H 0 (invD (dy n τ f t)) ∧ hn 0 (invD (dy n τ f t)) ≤ C*q ∧
    H 0 (yn n τ f t) ∧ hn 0 (yn n τ f t) ≤ C*q ∧
    H (-pstar) (yn n τ f t) ∧ hn (-pstar) (yn n τ f t) ≤ C*τ*q
def stepControls (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 1 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ,
    ∀ f w : Coeff, stepHyp γ M τ f w → stepControlsAt γ C n τ f w
def residualControls (γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 1 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ τ : ℝ,
  ∀ f w : Coeff, stepHyp γ M τ f w →
    let a := (n:ℝ)*τ
    let b := ((n:ℝ)+1)*τ
    let q := τ^γ+hn 0 (f-w)
    boundedH 0 a b (rho n τ f) ∧ supH 0 a b (rho n τ f) ≤ C*τ*q ∧
    aeH (-pstar) a b (drho n τ f) ∧ essH (-pstar) a b (drho n τ f) ≤ C*q
def stability (T γ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ M : ℝ, 1 ≤ M → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
  ∀ q : Coeff, ∀ u : Curve, solution 1 γ T q u → smoothCurve 0 T u →
    1+supH γ 0 T (twisted 1 u) ≤ M →
  ∀ τ : ℝ, 0 < τ → τ ≤ 1 →
  ∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → b ≤ T → b-a ≤ 1 →
    (∃ n : ℕ, a = (n:ℝ)*τ) →
    let e := twisted 1 u - interp τ q
    let E := supH 0 a b e
    E ≤ 1 → ∀ N : ℝ, 2 ≤ N →
      E ≤ hn 0 (e a)+C*(b-a+τ)*τ^γ+
        C*(N^2*(b-a)+(b-a)+τ+N⁻¹+N^(-pstar))*E
def gridRate (T γ C τ0 : ℝ) (q : Coeff) (u : Curve) : Prop :=
  ∀ L : ℕ, 0 < L →
    let τ := T/(L:ℝ)
    τ ≤ τ0 → ∀ n : ℕ, n ≤ L →
      H 0 (iter τ q n) ∧
      hn 0 (u ((n:ℝ)*τ)-iter τ q n) ≤ C*τ^γ
def smoothRate (T γ R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C τ0 : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < τ0 ∧
    ∀ q : Coeff, rd γ q → smooth q → hn γ q ≤ R →
    (∃ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u) ∧
    (∀ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u →
      gridRate T γ C τ0 q u ∧
      ∀ L : ℕ, 0 < L →
        let τ := T/(L:ℝ)
        τ ≤ τ0 → supH 0 0 T (twisted 1 u - interp τ q) ≤ C*τ^γ)
def rate (T γ R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C τ0 : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < τ0 ∧
    ∀ q : Coeff, rd γ q → hn γ q ≤ R →
    (∃ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u ∧
      ∀ v : Curve, exact 1 γ T q v → EqOn u v (Icc 0 T)) ∧
    (∀ u : Curve, exact 1 γ T q u → gridRate T γ C τ0 q u)
end KdV

For the real mean-zero 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, with normalized homogeneous norms, the following results hold in its norm-preserving twisted representation. For every s>=0, time horizon A>0 and L2 upper bound B0, Galerkin solutions with datum q in dot H^s and ||q||_2<=B0 obey sup_[0,A]||U_m||_(dot H^s)<=M_s, uniformly in m, with M_s depending only on s,A,B0,||q||_(dot H^s). For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,A];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L^infty dot H^s to a distributional solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique, is C([0,A];dot H^s), preserves L2 at every time and depends Lipschitz continuously on the datum for s>1/2, and also for 0<s<=1/2. At s=0 there is a unique C([0,A];L2) solution with Lipschitz dependence obtained by smoothing. For theta in (-1,0] and two data q,r in L2 whose norms sum to at most B0, the two twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,A]||Utw-Vtw||_(dot H^theta)<=C' C_(B0)^A ||q-r||_(dot H^theta), where C',C_(B0) depend only on B0,theta.

source.statement: For every smooth mean-zero f, tau>0 and nonnegative integer n, let t_n=n*tau and let q=S_(t_n)f. With the displayed Li-Wu maps F_tau,H_tau, its algebraic step identity is S_(-t_n-tau)[S_tau q+F_tau(q)+H_tau(q)]=f+Stage_(n,tau)(t_n+tau;f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Stage_(n,tau)(s;f))ds-R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f). The R2 has exactly the Fourier phase covariance, sign and coefficient of D012, including zero output.

E001.explanation: Fourier identification uses the normalized measure dx/(2π) on the same 2π torus. dh/dn are exactly mean-zero homogeneous H^s membership/norm; contH in the inhomogeneous norm has the identical topology by the two-sided weight comparisons on |k|≥1. The sign=-1 coefficient equation is U_t=UU_x+U_xxx, since (ik)^3=-ik³; twisted (-1) is its norm-preserving e^(+itk³) source twist. bit retains uniform Galerkin bounds and uniform limiting-flow bounds with constants chosen before every datum in the prescribed norm bounds, Galerkin subsequences strongly in each finite L^p H^σ and weak-star in L∞ dot H^s, existence/uniqueness/continuity, conservation, H^s Lipschitz dependence, the s=0 smooth-approximation flow and the full theta∈(-1,0] exponential-in-time dependence. The strong L^p condition is convergence of the integral of the pth power of the norm; weak-star is testing the Fourier dual pairing against every Bochner L¹ dot H^(-s) path. These characterize precisely those convergence modes in the separable weighted ℓ² model, in both directions. A common bound can be enlarged to cover Galerkin and limiting solutions, so separate existential bound variables do not change uniformity. Curves are identified only on the declared horizon. All appearances of exact impose the solution relation rather than assuming it. Reflection/sign transfer to the target is proved in T001, not built into this premise.

E002.explanation: cint is the Fourier form of D015 with both projections and the inverse derivative in the third input; constant paths implement the time-independent clause. srcScale=√(2π) multiplies every normalized H^r or L² norm, including both summands of X, yielding precisely Li-Wu's unnormalized norms. cubicBounds at this scale quantifies alpha∈[0,1], every 0≤a≤b with b-a≤1, and every admissible triple, with the negative-norm factor allowed in each Fin 3 slot and the product over the other two. The first constant is chosen before the interval and paths; the constant-input constant may depend on s. aeH and weakD express the given L∞ regularity and weak time derivative through their absolutely continuous coefficient representatives; changing a representative on a null set does not change any integral or essential norm. Weighted ℓ² separability identifies coordinate measurability plus membership with Bochner measurability. Conversely these norm/weak-derivative data give exactly such representatives. H 0 on the output records that the asserted L² bound is a bound on an actual L² object. Normalization is performed in T006, not silently absorbed by changing this premise.

E003.explanation: Spatial multiplication is convolution of normalized coefficients, with output H 0 membership and the L² estimate both asserted. productBounds retains every sigma∈[0,1] and every fixed epsilon>0; sourceAux is 1/2+epsilon at zero, 1/2-sigma below the midpoint, epsilon at the midpoint, and zero above it. Each norm is multiplied by √(2π), exactly the source normalization. The constant may depend on sigma and the fixed epsilon but is independent of the input functions. This is the same product inequality in both Fourier and physical models, without a mean-zero restriction on either input.

E004.explanation: stage is one half of the coefficient integral of B_s(f,g) from n tau to t. stageBounds preserves all 0<sigma≤1, every beta in the closed interval [beta0,1+sigma], n≥0, tau>0 and the entire step, on time-independent mean-zero H^sigma inputs. beta0 has exactly the three source formulas. At sigma=1/2 the phrase 'any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0' is encoded as existence of epsilon0>0 followed by every 0<epsilon<epsilon0; its constant may depend on that fixed epsilon and beta, never on the state, n, tau or support. Away from the midpoint beta0 is independent of epsilon and is encoded with epsilon=0 only as an unused argument. The time exponent is exactly (1+sigma-beta)/(1+sigma-beta0) and all norms carry √(2π). The Fourier integral and physical stage agree coefficientwise; the estimate asserts H^beta membership, so it is also the bounded extension described by the source.

E005.explanation: schemeIdentity is the exact source algebraic identity in the common Fourier representation: q=S_(n tau) f, and air(-n tau-tau)(step tau q) is the twisted physical update. quad and cubic expand D008-D009 exactly, including S_(s-tau) in the final endpoint product and the outer inverse second derivative. rem uses zero output at k=0, excludes a+b=0, and has exactly -tau/(18 i k), exp(-i n tau Phi) and eta_tau with alpha=3ab(a+b), beta=3kc(a+b). Summing over a,b with c=k-a-b is a bijective reindexing of a+b+c=k, including all zero input modes, whose phases cancel. The right side is f+Stage+integral B(f,Stage)-R2. Smooth mean-zero inputs, all tau>0 and all natural n are retained, with no support restriction.

P.explanation: Together with H001-H003 the parameters are exactly T>0, 0<gamma≤1 and R>0. rate chooses C>0 and tau0>0 before every real mean-zero H^gamma datum q of norm≤R and before L, so the constants depend only on T,gamma,R. It includes existence and uniqueness, on [0,T], of the continuous H^gamma distributional solution obtained from smooth Fourier-cutoff solutions in uniform L²; uniqueness is in precisely that solution class. For every such solution and every natural L>0 with tau=T/L≤tau0, gridRate asserts H^0 membership of each numerical iterate and the norm error at every n≤L, including n=0. This is equivalent to the displayed maximum over the nonempty finite grid. iter is the explicitly expanded fixed Li-Wu step, with no spatial cutoff and no numerical H^gamma hypothesis. hn 0 is exactly the normalized physical L² norm by the specified Fourier-completion convention; in the other direction each physical datum/solution and scheme has precisely these coefficient sequences and equality/norm bounds. Equation identification uses the coefficient integral formulation of the distributional equation; continuity and L² products justify testing individual modes and recovering all smooth periodic tests. The smooth-approximation convention is witnessed and never made an extra hypothesis on the datum. T012 performs the fixed-timestep limiting argument, preserving the constants and all quantifiers.

value.statement: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique distributional solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) obtained by smooth approximation and the fixed unfiltered iterates of Psi satisfy max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_L2<=C*tau^gamma for every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. The constants are uniform over that entire datum ball and all these L; no Fourier-support restriction is imposed.

H s is weighted square summability with weight (1+k²)^s, and hn is the square root of that sum; dh/dn are the homogeneous versions restricted away from zero. This is exactly the completion-of-polynomials model in D003, including negative orders. contH and convH state continuity/convergence in these weighted norms, not pointwise coefficient topology. smooth means membership in every nonnegative integer Sobolev space, equivalent to a smooth periodic function; smoothCurve and smoothPair express norm continuity and C¹ dependence at every such order. All displayed series and integrals are mathematical noncomputable definitions; consumers must establish the guarded summability, integrability and boundedness, which are included in the output obligations when substantive. No default tsum or sSup value is used as an analytic conclusion without the appropriate domain. mul is spatial multiplication in coefficients, air is S_t, and invD is zero on mode zero. The unfiltered scheme and finite iterates are explicit formulas, with no unspecified solver or algebraic capabilities. weakD is the coefficientwise integrated weak derivative with the absolutely continuous representative. aeH supplies coefficient measurability, a.e. Hilbert membership and an essential bound; separability of weighted ℓ² identifies this with the usual Bochner L∞ condition. essH uses ENNReal essential supremum then toReal only on these bounded domains; xn uses essential norms, while supH concerns actual continuous value representatives. piecewise allows separate derivative extensions at knots and identifies the global derivative only a.e. on each piece. solution uses the physical normalized equation's coefficient integral identity; for s≥0 C H^s this is equivalent to the distributional equation because the L² product has absolutely convergent convolution coefficients. exact adds uniform-in-time L² convergence from smooth solutions for the Fourier cutoffs of q, expressing the fixed smooth-approximation solution convention without granting existence. Uniqueness is EqOn on [0,T], so arbitrary values of a Curve outside its horizon never affect the result. sign=1 denotes target u_t+u_xxx=∂x(u²)/2, sign=-1 denotes the source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx; this is an actual equation-sign parameter, not a regularity assumption. No M ports or background-note premises are introduced. Native type probes verified these complete predicates with no missing parameters. The ℝ powers in the weights and estimates are Real.rpow; natural powers of complex Fourier multipliers are ordinary monoid powers. The membership predicate uses real Summable rather than overloading an lp parameter: the inspected Memℓp definition uses an ENNReal exponent (zero means finite support and infinity means boundedness), so neither is silently used as Sobolev order. All frequency indices and grid indices are explicitly ℤ and ℕ respectively; n≥0 is intrinsic to ℕ, and L>0 is a proposition, not a truncated integer division. Complex scalar action on coefficients is pointwise; real coefficients in scalar actions are explicitly cast to ℂ.

steps.explanation: Exact-flow transfer. Apply E001 to the sign-reflected coefficients -q(-k), preserving reality, zero mean and every homogeneous norm. Check the inverse reflection and the physical equation's linear sign, then compare homogeneous and inhomogeneous weights on k≠0, in both exponent directions. For a smooth datum use all positive integer regularities and uniqueness. Unimodularity proves the twist norm identity and differentiating smooth solutions gives weakD of the twist with B/2. Establish the single ball bound before quantifying q. For arbitrary L² pairs apply θ=0 dependence and undo the unitary twists/reflection; the L² constant depends only on T and the summed norm bound.

Prove the scalar covariance estimates by cancellation, the fundamental theorem of calculus and either integration by parts, retaining both phase ratios. For a nonzero zero-sum quartet prove the ordered-magnitude cases, including ties. List.Perm plus the displayed inequalities states precisely what an ordering means; all denominators here are nonzero. The max/min formula k3 used in the next node is exactly the third largest magnitude, even with ties.

Dyadically decompose nonnegative sequences supported away from zero. For each ordering, the largest two shell indices differ by at most two. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the large pair and the cardinalities of the small shells produce 2^(-(j3-j4)/2) after division by the third largest frequency. Sum the geometric factor and the finitely many orderings/offsets. Pass from finite restrictions by monotone convergence. Summability and the bound are asserted together for each arbitrary subset Ω, avoiding the default value of an unsummable real tsum.

Combine T002's two multiplier majorants by geometric interpolation for 0≤s≤1; duality and T003 give the uniform trilinear estimate with any modulus≤1 multiplier, including either resonance restriction. Prove absolute coefficient summability and complex trilinearity, then density gives the unique bounded extension from polynomial inputs. The finite formula and its extension therefore use the same rem definition. Finally telescope the diagonal cubic at f around w: use exponent gamma only at (w,w,w) and exponent zero on the difference terms. No H^gamma norm of f is assumed.

Fourier isometry and elementary inverse-derivative, H¹ embedding and product estimates supply linearBounds, with H membership of each output explicit. Products denote convolution, justified by Cauchy-Schwarz or absolute summability of inverse-derivative coefficients. For the normal form differentiate the phase on smooth inputs, prove the coefficient identity, and integrate retaining both endpoints. For piecewise paths sum over a finite partition; derivatives are only identified a.e. with the piecewise extensions, so jumps do not require a common endpoint derivative. Prove symmetry, the cubic integral identity without commuting a product through an operator, and the constant-input stage identity.

Normalize E002 by srcScale=√(2π), including the value and derivative components of X; its alpha=0 instance is exactly the normalized variable-path bound. E003 with epsilon=1/8 and gamma>0 gives the chosen aux exponent and product estimate. Choose a single admissible sufficiently small epsilon_stage≤1/8 for the midpoint application of E004, before any state or step is chosen. Check the three beta0 cases and positive denominators: beta=aux gamma yields a time power at least gamma and beta=1+gamma yields power zero. Since 0<tau≤1 the weaker tau^gamma estimate follows. Constants are uniform in interval position, n, tau and support.

From E005 and the explicitly defined physical update, prove the twisted endpoint identity and preservation of smoothness, reality and mean zero. Check the S_(s-tau) factor in the last endpoint term. Differentiate the interpolation on each step, expand V=z+Y, and identify the actual residual derivative drho. Prove weakD for the concatenated paths, continuity and finite piecewise smoothness, both grid values, Y's initial zero value, and the concatenated residual increments. idx uses floor(t/tau) for nonnegative times; at grid endpoints either adjacent formula agrees by the proved endpoint identities.

Under the stated step hypothesis put q=tau^gamma+‖f-w‖₂≤2. T005's endpoint stage formula gives the uniform H¹ bound and the H¹ difference from Stage(w); T006 gives the small low-regularity norm. Split the derivative of the exact-data square using the product estimate, and control the square difference in H¹. T004 bounds the actual numerical-state remainder in W. Split f=w+(f-w) to bound Dinv B(f,F), integrate Y' from its initial zero value, and use the cubic normal form for C_n with the time-independent and mixed exponent-zero bounds. All displayed H memberships, admissibility and X bounds follow from these estimates and smooth step data.

Apply the existing normal form to (Y,z) and then (Y,Y), retaining both endpoints. Use T008's Dinv Y and Dinv Y' bounds with the asymmetric J estimate, and T006's negative-slot cubic estimate for the differentiated z term. Bound q² by 2q. The affine W contribution is the actual W of the interpolation. This gives the L² bound for rho; the negative-norm bilinear estimate applied directly to drho gives its essential derivative bound. No global residual is substituted for the step formula.

Take any smooth solution of the normalized equation, twist it and differentiate its coefficient equation. For e=v-V establish e'=B(e,v-e/2)-Rres' and the X bounds under E_I≤1. Sum actual step residual increments, allowing a final partial step. Split the integrated bilinear error at real frequency N≥2. Low output costs N²h. At high output apply the normal form retaining the initial endpoint; rewrite differentiated terms as the two Cint terms and the integral of J(Rres',V). Split each cubic input at N/3; all-low input frequencies cannot reach output >N, while each designated high slot has negative norm ≤C N^(-23/14) times its L² norm. Treat the forcing integral with the actual stepwise drho, Y and W bounds. Combine to obtain exactly the stated conditional stability inequality. The constant is uniform for solutions with 1+sup‖v‖_(H^gamma)≤M and depends only on T,gamma,M.

Use T001's common ball bound, and the normalized smooth equation required by T010. Choose N first to absorb its reciprocal powers, then a block length delta and tau≤delta/2. On blocks of floor(delta/tau) grid steps iterate the absorbed inequality. Continuity from T007 and the exact flow supports the first-hitting-time contradiction; the estimate also covers a prefix ending inside a step. Choose tau0 uniformly so the resulting K tau0^gamma<1/2. The interpolation bound implies the grid bound by the actual grid identity and isometry. The constants are chosen before any smooth datum or positive integer L.

Approximate q by low m q, preserving reality, mean zero and the H^gamma ball. T001 gives exact solutions converging uniformly in L². For each fixed tau>0 prove continuity in L² of the fully specified step using T005's inverse-derivative and H¹ product bounds; then all finitely many iterates converge. Apply T011 with the same constants to every cutoff datum. Pass the reverse triangle inequality at all n≤L and then their finite maximum. Retain existence and uniqueness in the smooth-approximation solution class. Constants precede q and L; no numerical Sobolev bound or cutoff is introduced into the method.
